# Total.js knowledge: every page

> Total.js 5 knowledge in one place: the conventions (ES5 first, Total.js prototypes and Tangular first, no imports from Node.js, pipe-separated action names, routes in controllers or in the plugin) and small complete applications, tested, that show them at work.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/README.md

# knowledge

Total.js 5 knowledge for AI models: small complete applications, examples and answers that follow the conventions, tested and ready to learn from.

[Totem](https://github.com/totaljs-es/totem) is the first model that learns from it. Any model, and any person, can use it.

## What is here

| Folder | Content |
|---|---|
| [`conventions/`](conventions) | How Total.js 5 applications are written, one page per subject: [general](conventions/general), [backend](conventions/backend), [database](conventions/database) and [frontend](conventions/frontend) |
| [`apps/`](apps) | Small complete applications. Each one starts, has its tests and says in its `readme.md` the request it answers and why it has that shape |
| [`answers/`](answers) | Short answers to the questions people ask about Total.js 5, each with its code and the application that shows it at work |
| [`questions/`](questions) | One question and its short answer, 224 of them by subject, in English, in Spanish ([`questions/es/`](questions/es)) and in Slovak ([`questions/sk/`](questions/sk), a draft until a native speaker reviews it) with the same code |
| [`reference/components/`](reference/components) | The 348 published jComponent components: the catalogue with what each one does and the page of each one, copied from its repository |
| [`reference/icons.md`](reference/icons.md) | The names of Total Icons |
| [`reference/`](reference) | What each version of Total.js 5 adds, tried with that version ([0.0.20](reference/total5-0.0.20.md), the beta), and the official guides of [jComponent 20](reference/jcomponent/readme.md): `ui-component`, `ui-bind`, `ui-plugin`, `ui-import`, the API and how to write a component |
| [`skills/`](skills) | Two skills for agents: write Total.js 5 code, and review a change |
| [`tools/`](tools) | `check.js` checks application files against the rules a script can decide, `rules.js` prints the rules, `test.js` runs the tests of every application |
| `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` | The index of the pages and every page in one file, for models |
| `knowledge.json` | For a program that searches these pages: the API names and the words of the headings of each one |

| Application | Shape | Storage |
|---|---|---|
| [`apps/contacts`](apps/contacts) | An API without plugins, with a token | `DATA` (QueryBuilder) on the embedded NoSQL database |
| [`apps/contacts-postgresql`](apps/contacts-postgresql) | The same API with its data in PostgreSQL: the same queries, without the prefix `nosql/` | `DATA` (QueryBuilder) on PostgreSQL |
| [`apps/files`](apps/files) | An API to upload and download files, with a token | `FILESTORAGE` |
| [`apps/monitor`](apps/monitor) | Work on a schedule: it checks websites every few minutes and says which ones are down | `MEMORIZE` |
| [`apps/website`](apps/website) | A website without plugins: views and a layout rendered on the server | A list in memory |
| [`apps/chat`](apps/chat) | A chat room over a WebSocket, with a page in jComponent 20 | In memory |
| [`apps/board`](apps/board) | An application with plugins: each feature has its routes, actions, screen and form (jComponent 20) | `DATA` (QueryBuilder) on the embedded NoSQL database |

## Use it

**Any model or agent:** give it [`llms.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/llms.txt) (the index) or [`llms-full.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/llms-full.txt) (everything), or add this line to the `AGENTS.md` of your project: "Follow the Total.js 5 knowledge of https://github.com/totaljs-es/knowledge". [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) has the rules; `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` point to it.

**Claude Code**, as a plugin: the two skills, a check after each edit and the rules at the start of a session in a Total.js project.

```
/plugin marketplace add totaljs-es/knowledge
/plugin install totaljs@totaljs-knowledge
```

**Codex**, as a plugin: the two skills.

```
codex plugin marketplace add totaljs-es/knowledge
codex plugin add totaljs
```

## The rules of everything here

- **It runs.** An application enters when it starts and its tests pass. `npm test` runs them all.
- **Total.js 5 and jComponent 20**, as the [conventions](conventions) say.
- **ES5 first**: `var` and `function`. `const` or `let` only where the code needs it, as a constant at the top of a file. `async` / `await` only where the code waits for the database (`await NOSQL(...).promise($)`).
- **Routes** are in `controllers/`, or in the `index.js` of the plugin when the application has plugins. Never inside the action.
- **Actions** are named `Collection|verb`, with a pipe.
- **Data** goes through `DATA` (QueryBuilder) from the start, with SQL names and the prefix `nosql/` on the embedded database (`DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact')`), so an application moves to PostgreSQL without writing its queries again. `NOSQL()`, `MEMORIZE()` and `FILESTORAGE()` are for what they are made for: see [storage](conventions/backend/storage-and-integrations.md).
- **Settings** are in the file `config`, and `total5` is `latest` in `package.json`.
- **`index.js`** is always the official start script of Total.js 5, whole and unchanged ([`helpers/index.js`](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/master/helpers/index.js) of the framework). It is the one file that keeps its own style.
- **No real data**: names, emails and tokens are invented.

## Run the tests

```
npm install
npm test
```

It checks the files for agents, the links of every page, the check itself and the applications. `apps/contacts-postgresql` needs PostgreSQL and a database for tests (`createdb knowledge_test`); without it, it is reported as skipped. After a page changes, `npm run llms` writes `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` again.

# AGENTS.md

This repository is the knowledge of Total.js 5 for agents and models: the conventions, and small complete applications that show them at work. Read it before writing or changing Total.js code.

## How to use it

1. Read the rules below. They apply to every change.
2. Open the pages of the zone you work in: `conventions/general/`, `conventions/backend/`, `conventions/database/` or `conventions/frontend/`. Start with `conventions/general/workflow.md` when choosing a pattern or correcting existing code.
3. Look at the application with the shape you need in `apps/`: its `readme.md` says the request it answers and why it has that shape.
4. In an existing project, copy the pattern of its nearest working feature; use these pages to decide what is idiomatic.

## Rules that apply to every change

- Total.js 5 only. Do not use Total.js 4 APIs. The interface is jComponent 20.
- `"total5": "latest"` is the stable version. Before using something that only a beta has (see `reference/`), check the version the project depends on and say which version it needs.
- ES5 first: `var`, `function`, classic loops, `'{0}'.format()` instead of template literals, no arrow functions. `const` or `let` only where the code needs it, as a constant at the top of a file; inside a function write `var`. `async` / `await` where the code waits for the database.
- `index.js` is always the official start script of Total.js 5, whole and unchanged (see `conventions/general/project-structure.md`). It is the one file that keeps its own style.
- Use Total.js prototypes (`findItem`, `format`, `parseJSON`, `slug`, `isEmail`...) in the backend and Tangular templates in the frontend before any other function.
- In initialized app code, do not `require()` exposed Node.js modules: use `Total.Fs`, `Total.Path`, `Total.Crypto`, `Total.Os`, `Total.Zlib`, etc.
- Settings are in the file `config` (not `config.json`, not environment variables), read with `CONF`. `total5` is the dependency in `package.json`, as `latest`.
- Actions are named `Collection|verb` with a pipe: `Tickets|list`, `Reports|Categories|list`. Never `/` or `\` in an action or schema name.
- Routes are in `controllers/`, or in the `index.js` of the plugin when the application has plugins. An existing application that declares `route:` in its actions keeps its style; never register the same endpoint twice.
- An application that will grow by features is made with plugins; a small API or a website with a few pages is not. See the applications of `apps/`.
- Loaded application modules are accessed through `MODS`, shared helpers hang from `FUNC` and shared state from `MAIN`.
- Keep the storage of an existing application. In a new one the records go through `DATA` (QueryBuilder) from the start, with SQL names: `DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact')` on the embedded NoSQL database, and the same table without the prefix `nosql/` when it moves to PostgreSQL; `NOSQL()` is for an embedded store that will never be SQL, `MEMORIZE()` for a small named object, `FILESTORAGE()` for files. In request queries use `.promise($)` / `.callback($)`; ids are `UID()`, dates are `NOW`.
- Preserve URLs, permissions, input and output shapes, settings keys and model paths during a style correction. Do not add an abstraction when a direct native call fits.
- Frontend: match the jComponent major version of the application; use an existing component before writing one; load catalogue components with `COMPONENTATOR()`.
- Every text for people is `@(Text)`, in English.
- Tabs, semicolons, `'` for short strings, lowercase file names with `-`.
- After editing JavaScript run `node --check file.js`; start the application and call the route you changed. Do not say that tests passed when the project has none.

## Layout

- `conventions/`: the pages, one folder per zone (`general/`, `backend/`, `database/`, `frontend/`).
- `apps/`: small complete applications, each with its `readme.md` and its `test.js`.
- `answers/`: short answers to common questions (how to start an application, where the routes go, which storage, plugins or not...), each with its question in English and in Spanish.
- `questions/`: one question and its short answer, by subject (`actions.md`, `routes.md`, `data.md`...). `questions/es/` and `questions/sk/` have the same pages in Spanish and in Slovak: the same sections in the same order and the same code, only the text is translated.
- `reference/`: what each version of Total.js 5 adds, tried with that version, `reference/jcomponent/`, the official guides of the interface library, `reference/components/`, the catalogue of the published components with the page of each one, and `reference/icons.md`, the names of the icons (copies and lists made from their sources, not edited here: `node scripts/components.js` updates them). Before writing a piece of interface by hand, look for a component in the catalogue; use only the icons of the list. A feature of a beta is used only in a project that depends on that version.
- `llms.txt` (index), `llms-full.txt` (every page in one file) and `knowledge.json` (the API names and the words of the headings of each page, for a program that searches them): they are generated with `npm run llms`, do not edit them by hand.
- `scripts/llms.js`: builds the two files above and lists the pages in order.
- `skills/`: the skills to write and to review Total.js 5 code (`.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` point to them).
- `tools/check.js`: checks application files against the rules a script can decide. `tools/rules.js` prints the rules above. `tools/test.js` runs the tests of every application.
- `hooks/hooks.json`: for the plugin, the check after each edit and the rules at the start of a session in a Total.js project.
- `.claude-plugin/` makes the repository a Claude Code plugin; `.codex-plugin/` and `.agents/plugins/` make it a Codex plugin.
- `tests/`: tests of the files for agents, of the check and of the links of the pages.

## Using this knowledge from another project

Point your agent at `llms.txt` (an index with a link to every page) or at `llms-full.txt` (all the pages at once):

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/llms.txt
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/llms-full.txt

A project can add a line to its own `AGENTS.md`: "Follow the Total.js 5 knowledge of https://github.com/totaljs-es/knowledge".

## Plugins and check

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add totaljs-es/knowledge`, then `/plugin install totaljs@totaljs-knowledge`. It adds the two skills, the check after each edit and the rules at the start of a session.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add totaljs-es/knowledge`, then `codex plugin add totaljs`. It adds the two skills.

Check files by hand: `node tools/check.js <file|directory>` (`--strict` makes style findings fail, `--json` prints JSON). It only checks files inside a project that depends on `total5`, in the Total.js folders (`schemas/`, `controllers/`, `definitions/`, `modules/`, `plugins/`, `actions/`, `views/`).

## Checking this repository

- `npm test` checks the files for agents, that every page is listed in `llms.txt`, that `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` match the pages, that every link works, the check itself, and it runs the tests of every application.
- After you change or add a page, run `npm run llms` and `npm test`. A new page is also added to the list in `scripts/llms.js`.

## Keeping this knowledge true

Every rule here comes from code that exists, and every application here starts and passes its tests. When you add a rule, add an example from a real file or from the framework source, and say which. When you add an application, add its tests.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/general/workflow.md

# Writing and correcting Total.js apps

Use this workflow with the pages for the affected zone.

## Before writing

1. Read the target project's instructions, entry point, dependencies and nearest working feature. Identify the backend version, browser UI major, storage model and route registration pattern.
2. Select the nearest existing feature of the target project with the same storage model. Read its route, action, screen and form together.
3. Record the contracts you must preserve: URL and action ID, body/query/params, response envelope, permission IDs, settings keys and plugin/model paths.
4. Find the native helper or existing component before creating a wrapper. See [native patterns](native-patterns.md). Read only the component documentation compatible with the app's UI version.

## Write a feature

Implement the same direct flow as the reference: route → validated action → existing storage → one response, with the UI calling that endpoint and binding its result. Keep `exports`, `$`, `model`, `self`, `config`, `cls` and familiar field names. Add only the files the feature needs. Keep business checks in the action; input validation does not establish ownership or authorization.

For SQL-backed features follow [queries](../database/queries.md) and add the schema upgrade if needed. For memory/FileStorage features use the app's existing load/save and cache hooks. For UI changes follow [binding and forms](../frontend/binding-and-forms.md).

## Correct existing code

Review a bounded feature or diff. For each finding record:

| Field | What to record |
|---|---|
| Location | File and line, with the concrete code |
| Rule | Page and reference file that support the finding |
| Kind | Runtime/API defect, contract change, convention mismatch or optional simplification |
| Correction | Smallest change that fixes it and the callers it affects |
| Verification | Observable result that would demonstrate the fix |

Remove duplicated validation and pass-through wrappers when a native call expresses the same behaviour. Keep ownership/business checks, cancellation, error mapping and other behaviour that the native replacement does not supply. Do not replace all storage with SQL, migrate UI versions or split actions merely to satisfy an example in this guide. Correct action/schema separators to `|` by updating registrations and callers together; check generated endpoints and preserve public URL compatibility. URL paths and plugin method paths keep their own separators.

Make corrections by coherent feature, preserving owner changes. A formatting rewrite and an endpoint redesign have different review risks; keep their intent explicit. Do not edit minified vendor assets, bundles or runtime databases as source.

## Organize files during a refactor

Apply the [project structure](project-structure.md) policy: runtime files in recognizable Total.js folders, private runtime inputs under `private/`, and documentation, evaluation material and independent examples under `docs/`. The running application must not depend on `docs/`; development tools can use its fixtures. Consume automatically loaded modules through `MODS`, while preserving standalone-tool imports.

Before deleting an old tree, remove its runtime reader, routes, generators and obsolete checks together. Preserve contracts unless the requested scope explicitly retires them. Retain the current external integration when replacing local artifacts with an external source, and keep its integrity checks. Generated/minified dependencies and historical evidence must not be silently rewritten as part of a folder move.

Check package contents and private-file allowlists, temporary export layouts, migration inputs and documentation links after moving a file. An old layout may still be intentional input to a one-time legacy migration; document that exception instead of changing what the migration reads.

## Verify the result

- Run `node --check` for changed JS; it does not cover inline scripts in HTML, templates or browser APIs.
- Exercise the affected route with valid and invalid input, anonymous and authorized users, and insufficient permissions. For record operations also check a different owner's record and a missing ID.
- Confirm the response shape expected by the caller, not just a successful HTTP status.
- In the browser, open and reopen the screen/form, create/edit/cancel, submit and confirm caller refresh. Check the served asset and console when the UI changes; test release output if compilation/minification matters.
- Use existing project checks and focused regression tests where behaviour warrants them. Record exactly what ran and what could not run, including unavailable DB, credentials or browser access.

Finish with the concrete changes, evidence and remaining limitations. A successful documentation test only validates this reference's structure; it does not prove an app follows every convention or that its runtime works.

## Project instruction snippet

Add this to a consuming project's instructions when adopting this reference:

```text
Follow the Total.js 5 knowledge of https://github.com/totaljs-es/knowledge.
Read general/workflow.md and the pages for this change.
Use the nearest compatible Total.js example. Use | between parts of action
and schema names, never / or \. Update registrations and callers together
when correcting names, checking endpoint compatibility. Preserve URLs,
permissions, storage model and UI major version during corrections.
Keep runtime inputs in private/, internal documentation and examples in docs/,
and loaded application module access through MODS. Preserve standalone-tool
imports and update package/test/export paths when moving files.
Report convention findings with file/line, rule, proposed fix and checks run.
```

## Documentation and AI kits

Keep deliverable documentation limited to contracts, setup, commands and verified limits. Do not include personal names, internal conversations, tool provenance or incidental machine details. Choose the smallest useful structure and follow the target's examples; adding an authoring kit does not authorize rewriting its catalogue.

For reusable AI guidance, use one maintained workflow per skill and pointers for the supported agents. Keep documentation indexes generated and tested. Include compatible examples and artifact-specific checks. Follow [native testing](testing.md) for the runner, dependencies and integration boundaries, and [CMS widgets](../frontend/cms-widgets.md) when the deliverable is a widget rather than a jComponent.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/general/native-patterns.md

# Prefer direct native patterns

Operations go directly in actions and plugin methods, with shared behaviour in `FUNC` or a dedicated integration module. There is no service/repository/DTO stack for each feature.

## Choose the existing operation

| Need | First choice | Avoid introducing merely for indirection |
|---|---|---|
| Typed request | `input`, `params`, `query`, shared `@Schema` | A second validator for the same type checks |
| Find a cached item | `items.findItem('id', id)` | A one-use lookup service |
| Query SQL | `DATA.read/find/list/insert/modify/remove` | A repository class mirroring the builder |
| Outgoing HTTP | `RESTBuilder` | A fetch/axios wrapper that duplicates existing transport |
| App paths | `PATH.root/public/databases/temp` | Hard-coded machine paths or a new path resolver |
| App files and metadata | Existing `FILESTORAGE`, `MEMORIZE`, `FUNC.load/save` | A new persistence backend for the same data |
| Shared business operation | Existing action or a small `FUNC.name` | Forwarding through several functions without adding behaviour |
| UI state and calls | `PLUGIN`, model paths, `exports.tapi`, components | A second state store or HTTP client |
| UI events | `exec` and plugin methods | Separate event wiring for standard buttons |

These are selection defaults, not a ban on helpers. A helper earns its place by expressing a reused operation or isolating an integration, not by forwarding the same arguments. Keep names and object shapes familiar to the surrounding app.

## Input is already typed; business rules still matter

Example:

```js
NEWACTION('Redirects|read', {
	name: 'Read redirect',
	input: '*id',
	permissions: 'redirects,admin',
	action: function($, model) {
		var item = MAIN.db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
		if (item)
			$.callback(item);
		else
			$.invalid(404);
	}
});
```

Do not reparse `model.id` or add an alternative success envelope. In a user-owned feature, also constrain the lookup to the owner or tenant using the target app's existing rule.

## Know the execution context

`Total.*`, `DATA`, `NOW` and prototypes are available after framework initialization; browser `SET`/`PLUGIN` APIs belong to the loaded UI library. A standalone Node script must initialize what it needs. Never replace a tool's valid Node import with an unavailable app global.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/general/project-structure.md

# Project structure

A Total.js 5 app is a folder that the framework loads by convention. Put each kind of file where the framework (and the next reader) expects it.

```
index.js            starts the app: the official start script, whole (see below)
config              settings, one "key : value" per line
package.json        "total5" is the runtime dependency
controllers/        routes: exports.install = function() { ROUTE(...) }
definitions/        auth.js, init.js, func.js, db.js: loaded at start, no exports
modules/            integrations with other systems (cdn, tapi...)
plugins/<name>/     a feature: index.js (server), index.html (UI), schemas/, public/
schemas/            actions that are not part of a plugin
views/              layout and pages (HTML with @{...} directives)
public/             browser-accessible static files
private/            internal runtime files and grouped SQL/maintenance assets
docs/               development documentation, evidence and standalone examples
database.sql        the full schema; changes go to dated files next to it
```

Optional, when the app is shipped: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `bundle.sh` (writes `--bundles--/app.bundle`), `license.txt`, `readme.md`.

## Recognizable application folders

Runtime code and inputs belong in the framework folders above. Classify a file by its consumer, rather than creating a new top-level folder for every concern. `docs/` is for development material; the running application must not read it. Development tools may read evaluation fixtures and reference projects there.

Where things go:

| Material | Location | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| Enabled-language catalogue | `private/languages.json` | Application and validation tools |
| Interface translations | `resources/<lang>.resource` | Native localization |
| SQL, migration notes and maintenance units | `private/database/` | Startup, installation and maintenance |
| Evaluation fixtures and recorded checks | `docs/evaluations/` | Development tools and reviewers |
| Investigation reports and reproductions | `docs/findings/` | Developers |
| Standalone reference applications | `docs/examples/<name>/` | Readers and example checks |

A language catalogue is configuration data, not the interface translation store. Database-backed editorial translations remain in their existing database. Moving a file does not authorize a storage migration.

Use `public/` only when a browser or public client is intended to retrieve the file. Use `private/` for files the application needs internally. Exclude credentials, local databases and development documentation from deployment archives; whitelist the specific private paths required by the runtime rather than packaging the entire directory. Generated assets are not hand-edited source.

The root `database.sql` and dated upgrades remain valid existing layouts. When grouping internal SQL files, put the group under `private/database/` rather than creating an application-level `database/` folder.

## index.js

The start script is the same in every app: the official one of Total.js 5 ([`helpers/index.js`](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/master/helpers/index.js) of the framework), whole and unchanged. Do not write a shorter one by hand and do not restyle it: it is the one file that keeps its own style (`const`, `includes`). Its commented lines are the options that a project turns on later.

```js
// ===================================================
// Total.js v5 start script
// https://www.totaljs.com
// ===================================================

require('total5');

const options = {};

// options.ip = '127.0.0.1';
// options.port = parseInt(process.argv[2]);
// options.unixsocket = PATH.join(F.tmpdir, 'app_name.socket');
// options.unixsocket777 = true;
// options.config = { name: 'Total.js' };
// options.sleep = 3000;
// options.inspector = 9229;
// options.watch = ['private'];
// options.livereload = 'https://yourhostname';
// options.watcher = false; // disables watcher
// options.edit = 'wss://www.yourcodeinstance.com/?id=projectname'
// options.editmcp = 'https://yourtotalmcpserverinstance.com/?id=admin'

options.release = process.argv.includes('--release');

// Service mode:
options.servicemode = process.argv.includes('--service') || process.argv.includes('--servicemode');
// options.servicemode = 'definitions,modules,config';

// Cluster:
// options.tz = 'utc';
// options.cluster = 'auto';
// options.limit = 10; // max 10. threads (works only with "auto" scaling)

Total.run(options);
```

Run it with `node index.js 8000` (add `--release` for release mode).

## Where things go

- **A route** follows the app's existing pattern: `controllers/*.js` / plugin `index.js`, or the action's `route:` property.
- **Business logic** belongs in actions: usually `schemas/` or `plugins/<name>/schemas/`; compact plugins may declare actions in `index.js`.
- **Shared helpers** hang from `FUNC` (`FUNC.notify`, `FUNC.save`) and live in `definitions/func.js`.
- **Shared state in memory** hangs from `MAIN` (the app) or `REPO` (cached lookups, e.g. `REPO.tags`).
- **Startup work** (config defaults, loading caches, registering UI components) goes in `ON('ready', ...)` in `definitions/init.js`.
- **Authentication** is one `AUTH(...)` in `definitions/auth.js`.

## Files and folders

- All lowercase, words separated by `-`, never `_`: `search-results.html`.
- Static files by type: `/img/`, `/js/`, `/css/`, `/fonts/`, `/videos/`.
- One plugin per feature, named after the feature: `plugins/redirects`, `plugins/users`.
- Generated output (`--bundles--/`, `tmp/`, `databases/`) is not edited by hand.

## Checks

- `node --check path/to/file.js` for every JavaScript file you change.
- Start the app and call the route you touched. If the project has no test script, do not say tests passed.

After moving files, update runtime readers, exporters, migration tools, isolated-test setup, package allowlists, ignore rules and documentation links together. Preserve source content and recorded evidence. Verify that the archive includes the new runtime paths and excludes internal documentation and credentials.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/general/javascript-style.md

# JavaScript style

Three rules come first, because they decide most of the code you write:

1. **ES5 over ES6.** New code uses the ES5 form.
2. **Total.js first.** Use the framework's prototypes (backend) and Tangular (frontend) before any other function.
3. **No imports from Node.js.** Use the modules Total.js already exposes.

## 1. ES5 over ES6

Write `var`, `function`, classic loops and string helpers. Use an ES6 feature only when there is no ES5 way to do the same.

| Prefer | Instead of |
|---|---|
| `var item = ...;` | `let` / `const` in a function (at the top of a file they are fine when needed) |
| `function(item) { ... }` | `item => ...` |
| `for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++)` | long transformation chains or `for...of` in new examples |
| `'Hello {0}'.format(name)` | template literal `` `Hello ${name}` `` |
| `var a = obj.a;` | destructuring, spread, optional chaining |
| `arr.findItem('id', id)` | `arr.find(x => x.id === id)` |

```js
// good
var item = db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
if (!item) {
	$.invalid(404);
	return;
}

// avoid
const item = db.redirects.find(m => m.id === model.id);
```

Notes:

- `async` / `await` stays where the framework's own code uses it (`await DATA.find(...).promise($)`): there the ES5 alternative is a callback chain (`.callback($)`), which is also valid when it reads better.
- Existing code may use `let`, arrows, `for...of` and `async` functions. Do not rewrite unrelated working code merely to make an existing app look uniformly ES5.
- ES5 is the preference, not a prohibition. `const` and `let` are used when the project needs them, typically a constant at the top of a file (a definition, a module): `const ADMIN = { id: 'admin', sa: true };`. Inside a function write `var`.
- **Never `for...in` over an array**: it enumerates property names, including enumerable extensions, rather than just indexed values. Use a classic `for` loop.

## 2. Total.js first

### Backend: prototypes

Total.js extends `String`, `Array`, `Number` and `Date`. Before writing a helper, a loop or a regular expression, check whether a prototype does it. These exist in Total.js 5:

- **String:** `format`, `parseJSON`, `parseInt`, `parseFloat`, `parseBoolean`, `parseDate`, `parseConfig`, `parseCSV`, `parseXML`, `slug`, `capitalize`, `pluralize`, `max`, `toSearch`, `toKeywords`, `removeTags`, `encode`, `decode`, `safehtml`, `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `hash`, `crc32`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `isEmail`, `isPhone`, `isURL`, `isJSON`, `isUID`, `isGUID`, `isNumber`, `isBase64`, `isXSS`, `isSQLInjection`, `indent`, `tslash`.
- **Array:** `findItem`, `findIndex`, `findAll`, `findValue`, `remove`, `quicksort`, `trim`, `first`, `last`, `take`, `skip`, `limit`, `group`, `random`, `wait`, `async`.
- **Number:** `format`, `currency`, `round`, `floor`, `fixed`, `between`, `padLeft`, `padRight`, `filesize`, `pluralize`, `discount`, `parseDate`.
- **Date:** `format`, `add`, `diff`, `extend`, `toUTC`, `setTimeZone`, `parseDate`.

```js
var name = '{0} {1}'.format(first, last);                  // not a template literal
var index = items.findIndex('id', id);                     // not findIndex(m => m.id === id)
var data = text.parseJSON();                               // not try { JSON.parse(text) } catch
var slug = title.slug();                                   // not a hand-made regex
var keywords = body.toKeywords();
if (email.isEmail()) { ... }
```

If you are about to write a utility, search the framework source (`utils.js`) first. The helpers of `U.` (e.g. `U.normalize()`) and the globals (`UID()`, `NOW`, `CONF`, `DATA`) come before your own.

### Frontend: Tangular

In jComponent code and plugin HTML, build text and markup with **Tangular** templates (`{{ value }}`, `{{ foreach m in value }}`, `{{ if }}`) and its helpers, not with string concatenation or DOM-building code.

```html
<script type="text/html">
	{{ foreach m in value }}
	<figure class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}">{{ m.url }}</figure>
	{{ end }}
</script>
```

See [plugins-ui](../frontend/plugins-ui.md).

## 3. No imports from Node.js

Do not `require()` Node.js modules. Total.js exposes them:

| Instead of | Use |
|---|---|
| `require('fs')` | `Total.Fs` |
| `require('path')` | `Total.Path` |
| `require('crypto')` | `Total.Crypto` |
| `require('os')` | `Total.Os` |
| `require('http')` / `require('https')` | `Total.Http` / `Total.Https` (for requests prefer `RESTBuilder`) |
| `require('child_process')` | `Total.Child` |
| `require('zlib')` | `Total.Zlib` |
| `require('url')`, `require('util')`, `require('stream')` | `Total.Url`, `Total.Util`, `Total.Stream` |

Also available: `Total.Cluster`, `Total.Dns`, `Total.Net`, `Total.Tls`, `Total.Worker` and `Total.isBundle`. `Total.Os` is case-sensitive; `Total.OS` is not the exported property. For Node modules without a dedicated exposed property, use the global `REQUIRE('vm')` rather than inventing `Total.Vm`. In the reference implementation `REQUIRE` aliases `Total.require`; prefer the familiar global spelling in new code. Third-party packages are the last resort: the framework usually covers the need.

```js
// good
var file = PATH.temp('data.json');

// avoid
const Path = require('path');
```

In Total.js 5 use `Total.Path`, not `const Path = require('path')`.

Application files run after Total.js has initialized these globals. Bootstrap files still load `total5`, database adapters may need `require('querybuilderpg')`, and standalone Node.js tools (such as this repo's generator) use Node imports. Do not apply app-global rules to a process that has not loaded the framework.

Access application modules through `MODS.name` or `MODS['hyphenated-name']`, rather than repeatedly requiring their file path. Standalone tools may import a shared helper directly; requiring `total5` alone does not populate the module registry. See [definitions and modules](../backend/definitions-and-modules.md).

## Formatting

- Indent with **tabs** (width 4). No trailing white space.
- End every statement with `;`.
- Short strings in `'` apostrophes.
- A condition with one statement has no braces and no blank line:

```js
if (!item)
	return;

item && refresh();     // fine for a simple expression
```

## Variables and names

- Common names, the same in every project: `id`, `name`, `value`, `email`, `items` / `arr` (a collection), `item`, `tmp`, `dtcreated`, `dtupdated`.

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Files, folders | lowercase, `-` | `form-offer.html` |
| Actions | `Collection\|verb` (pipe; exposed to MCP as `Collection_verb`) | `Redirects\|save` |
| Schemas | plural, first letter upper case; `@Name` for a reusable input; `\|` separates nested names, never `/` or `\` | `NEWSCHEMA('Tickets', ...)`, `'@Reports\|Categories'` |
| API routes | lowercase, `_` between collection and verb | `tickets_create` |
| Plugins, components, `FUNC.`, `MAIN.`, `REPO.` keys | lowercase | `FUNC.refreshtags` |
| Table and column names | lowercase | `tbl_user`, `dtcreated` |

## Framework globals

Use the globals that exist instead of writing your own: `UID()` for identifiers, `NOW` for the current date, `CONF` for config, `DATA` for the database, `EMPTYARRAY` / `EMPTYOBJECT` for read-only defaults.

```js
model.id = UID();
model.dtcreated = NOW;
```

`NOW` is a framework-owned cached Date, not a fresh clock read on every access/action. Do not initialize or reassign it in actions/tests that already load Total.js. Consecutive actions can share the same timestamp, so timestamps alone do not establish insertion order, uniqueness or elapsed time. Use an explicit ordering key when the contract needs a strict sequence. The refresh interval is version-dependent: the reference Framework 5 `index.js` refreshes it in a service timer every 5000 ms.

Source: [Framework 5 index.js](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/7d2d553fc774090081b4e3b1ae75a52ef06b42b8/index.js) (NOW initialization/service refresh) and [global.js](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/7d2d553fc774090081b4e3b1ae75a52ef06b42b8/global.js) (REQUIRE alias). See [native tests](testing.md) for standalone suites.

## Comments

A comment says why, in one or two lines, above the code it explains. Do not narrate what the next line does.

## Dependencies

Avoid adding any. If the framework has a helper (`RESTBuilder`, `FILESTORAGE`, `U.*`, `DATA`, a prototype), use it.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/general/testing.md

# Native tests and development tools

Use the target project's test layout and runner. New Total.js test suites load the framework directly and use its test library:

```js
require('total5');
require('total5/test');

Test.push('Contract', function(next) {
	var value = '<strong>'.encode();
	Test.print('encodes HTML-like text', value === '&lt;strong&gt;' ? null : value);
	next();
});

Test.run();
```

`Test.print(label, error)` fails when error is truthy. A successful run must reach the final test count and exit with status 0. Verify that a deliberate failure exits nonzero; unexpected exceptions must not turn an incomplete run into a successful result. Do not catch an assertion's failure in the same block that is meant to catch an action rejection.

Load required dependencies normally (`require('total5')`, `require('total5/test')`, and the adapter where needed). Do not search machine-specific framework folders, silently replace a missing dependency, or skip mandatory tests because the framework is absent. Install the dependencies documented by the project.

After initialization use `Total.Fs`, `Total.Path`, `Total.Child` and the other exposed modules. For a Node module without a dedicated exported property, use `REQUIRE('vm')`, for example. Bootstrap and third-party package imports remain valid. A plain Node tool that deliberately does not initialize Total.js retains its Node imports; do not convert unrelated tooling just to change its style.

## Configuration and samples

Use one `config` or `config.json` for the settings the suite actually needs. A standalone suite can load a plain config explicitly:

```js
LOADCONFIG(Total.Fs.readFileSync(Total.Path.join(__dirname, 'config'), 'utf8'));
```

This does not load the consuming application's config, authentication or modules. Do not duplicate the same settings in config, config-test and config-example files. Test-only settings are not part of the copied action's runtime contract. Keep credentials out of commits and read suite settings through `CONF`, not custom environment lookups in actions.

Keep small setup/sample data in test.js when that is the project pattern. A fixtures directory is optional for substantial external samples, not a required abstraction. A shared runner is appropriate when it removes duplicated setup; do not reorganize an existing suite or move its per-action test inventory without a concrete reason.

## Database integration

Tests may use PostgreSQL and the same native `DATA` adapter as the application. These are database integration checks; they are not credential-free pure unit tests. Configure the adapter once on the default connection when the action uses that connection. Do not add a database-name option to every action just to make it testable.

Use a clean, disposable database dedicated to tests. Before any destructive setup, verify the actual database with `current_database()` and reject an unexpected target. Warn next to the test connection setting if tables will be dropped/recreated or their contents overwritten. Do not use the application's database or silently create/migrate its production schema. Keep setup portable; do not depend on a particular desktop PostgreSQL distribution.

Document dependencies, setup, the command, covered behaviors and any skipped integration groups. Distinguish native/database results from real-provider or browser verification. Remote-provider calls should be mocked or served locally for unit tests; explicitly selected integration tests may use real sources. A failed requested download is a failed check, not a reason to silently use another source.

## Browser and visual checks

Playwright can control its installed Chromium or an installed Chrome. Chromium is a portable default (`npx playwright install chromium`); selecting Chrome is optional and is not application configuration. Match the UI library used by the consuming application.

Verify behavior, two independent instances, repeated updates and desktop/mobile layout. Generate a screenshot of the final artifact and open it to assess appearance. A screenshot file's existence or passing DOM assertions does not establish visual quality. Keep isolated widget/component smoke tests distinct from testing the full editor/application and its published output.

## References

- [Framework 5 test.js](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/7d2d553fc774090081b4e3b1ae75a52ef06b42b8/test.js): Test.push, Test.print and Test.run.
- [Framework 5 global.js](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/7d2d553fc774090081b4e3b1ae75a52ef06b42b8/global.js): REQUIRE and framework globals.
- [CMS widget kit test.js](https://github.com/totaljs-es/cms-widgets/blob/63892ff/test.js), [config](https://github.com/totaljs-es/cms-widgets/blob/63892ff/tests/config), [browser tool](https://github.com/totaljs-es/cms-widgets/blob/63892ff/tools/browser.js): native runner, pinned sources and browser checks.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/backend/actions.md

# Actions

An action is one unit of server logic: a name, the input it accepts, who may call it, and a function. Define it with `NEWACTION` in a `schemas/` file.

```js
NEWACTION('Redirects|save', {
	name: 'Save redirect',
	input: 'id,*url,*target,permanent:Boolean',
	permissions: 'redirects,admin',
	action: function($, model) {

		if (model.id) {
			var item = MAIN.db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
			if (!item) {
				$.invalid(404);
				return;
			}
			item.dtupdated = NOW;
			item.url = model.url;
			item.target = model.target;
			item.permanent = model.permanent;
		} else {
			model.id = UID();
			model.dtcreated = NOW;
			MAIN.db.redirects.push(model);
		}

		FUNC.save();
		$.success();
	}
});
```

## Naming

`Collection|verb`, collection in plural and capitalized: `Tickets|list`, `Groups|create`, `Users|remove`. Separate the two parts with a pipe `|`.

Use `|` between parts of action and schema names, never `/` or `\`: `Tickets|list`, `Reports|Categories|list`, `@Reports|Categories`. A simple name such as `Tickets` or `@Group` needs no separator. This applies to grouped and nested names too.

Existing code may contain slash names; they are not the naming rule to reproduce. When correcting them, update registrations, route targets, `ACTION` / `$.action` calls and direct action-name `tapi()` calls together. Check automatically generated endpoint names and existing external callers; preserve public URLs with explicit routes or compatibility mappings where needed. Do not change URL path separators or plugin method paths such as `?/refresh`: this rule applies to action/schema names.

The framework's MCP sanitizer maps both `/` and `|` to `_`; the pipe convention is our naming choice, not an MCP requirement.

The usual verbs:

| Verb | Does | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | returns a collection, often with `autoquery` | query string |
| `read` | returns one record | `params: '*id:UID'` |
| `create` | inserts, answers with the new id | `input` |
| `update` | modifies one record | `params` + `input` |
| `save` | create or update by `id` | `input` with optional `id` |
| `remove` | deletes or flags one record | `params` |

Always give the action a human `name:` ("Save redirect"): it is used in logs and tools.

## Input and params

- `input:` is the body, `params:` is the route parameters (`{id}`), `query:` is the query string.
- A text spec: `'*name,color:Color,icon:Icon,permissions:[String]'`. A leading `*` makes a field required. After `:` goes the type (`Boolean`, `Number`, `UID`, `Email`, `Phone`, `Color`, `Date`, `String(100)`, `[String]`).
- Reuse a definition with a named schema and `@`:

```js
NEWSCHEMA('@Group', '*name,color:Color,icon:Icon,reference,permissions:[String]');

NEWACTION('Groups|create', {
	name: 'Create group',
	input: '@Group',
	action: async function($, model) { /* ... */ }
});
```

- Route parameters arrive in `$.params`, not as an argument: `$.params.id`.
- A list typed `*field:[String]` is required: an empty list counts as missing. If empty is valid, drop the `*`.

## Answering

| Call | Use |
|---|---|
| `$.callback(data)` | return data (a record, a list, an id) |
| `$.success()` / `$.success(id)` | the success answer of the app (`DEF.onSuccess`: by default `{ success: true }`, with the value if you pass one) |
| `$.invalid(404)` | not found; the number is the HTTP status |
| `$.invalid('@(Text for the user)')` | validation or business error; `@(...)` marks it for translation |

Complete each response path once. Use an early `return` when code would otherwise fall through after answering; a terminal callback does not need a redundant return. A delegated `.callback($)` or `.callback($.done(id))` also completes the action.

## Permissions

`permissions: 'redirects,admin'` uses the app's `UNAUTHORIZED` policy. Preserve the app's authorization mechanism: some actions use `permissions`, others `user: true`, `sa`, or an explicit `UNAUTHORIZED($, ...)` check. Authentication and access to a particular record are separate checks. Menu visibility grants no server access.

For a protected action that may also be called internally, declare the appropriate action-level check; the `+` on an HTTP route alone does not protect other invocation paths. `public: true` in reference code is not proof that an endpoint is anonymous; inspect the route and action checks. See `builders.js` action execution in the framework source.

## Options and calling

Beyond `input`, an action can declare `summary` (the description of the tool when it is exposed), `config` (defaults read as `$.config`), `output` (a filter: only the declared keys leave the action), `timeout`, `cache` and `mcp: true`. Callers override per call: `ACTION('Name', payload).config({}).env('test').user(user).promise()`. `.promise()` resolves with the answer and rejects with the error list. Standalone actions with tests: see [action kits](action-kits.md).

## Async and data

Actions are `async` when they await `DATA` calls. Pass `$` to `.promise($)` so errors answer the request for you:

```js
action: async function($) {
	var params = $.params;
	var model = await DATA.read('op.tbl_group').id(params.id).error('@(Group not found)').promise($);
	$.callback(model);
}
```

See [queries](../database/queries.md) for `DATA`.

## Calling one action from another

`$.action('Items|types').promise()` (or `ACTION('Items|types', model).promise()` outside a request). Keep shared pieces in an action instead of copying code.

## Grouped schemas are also Total.js 5

`NEWSCHEMA('Tickets', function(schema) { schema.action('list', { ... }); });`. Reusable input definitions and grouped actions are Total.js 5. Keep the target project's established form.

## Keep an action small

Split a repeated operation or a distinct responsibility when it improves readability. Length alone is not a reason to add a helper or an action chain. Large filter builders (e.g. a `makefilter($, builder)` function inside the schema) stay next to the actions that use them.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/backend/action-kits.md

# Standalone actions with tests

A kit is a repository of reusable actions that are not part of one application: one folder per action, with native tests. Pure parser tests need no network or credentials; SQL-backed actions may have explicitly configured database integration tests. An application copies the action, or loads it, and supplies the configuration.

## Layout

```
actions/<name>/
  action.js        one or more NEWACTION(), the folder is named after the provider or the topic (lower case)
  test.js          runs the actions with assertions
  config           test settings, only when needed
  init.sql         schema setup, only for SQL-backed actions
example/           the template: action.js and test.js
tools/check.js     checks structure and style, then runs test.js
```

Single files from an older layout (`actions/*.js`) stay as they are; a new action always has its folder and its test.

## Contract first

Name the action `Collection|verb` (see [actions](actions.md)) and write the contract before the code: `input`, `output`, `config` and the errors it returns. Split by responsibility:

- a `parse` action only transforms data it receives, no network;
- a `search` (or `read`, `send`, `ask`) action calls the provider and delegates the transformation to `parse` with `$.action('Shipments|parse', { data: response.body }).callback($)`.

The parser is tested with sample data, the caller with a local server. Keep small samples/setup inline; use separate fixture files only when their size or reuse justifies them. Match the existing repository rather than requiring a fixtures directory.

## action.js

```js
NEWACTION('Shipments|search', {
	name: 'Search shipments',
	summary: 'Searches shipments between two cities',
	input: '*from,*to,limit:Number',
	output: 'success:Boolean, items:[{ id:String, from:String, to:String, delay:Number }]',
	config: { url: 'https://api.example.com', token: '' },
	action: function($, model) {

		var opt = {};
		opt.method = 'GET';
		opt.url = $.config.url + '/shipments?from=' + encodeURIComponent(model.from) + '&to=' + encodeURIComponent(model.to);
		opt.headers = { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + $.config.token };
		opt.callback = function(err, response) {

			if (err || response.status !== 200) {
				$.invalid(err || response.status);
				return;
			}

			$.action('Shipments|parse', { data: response.body }).callback($);
		};

		REQUEST(opt);
	}
});

/*
	EXAMPLE:
	ACTION('Shipments|search', { from: 'Berlin', to: 'Vienna' }).config({ token: 'YOUR_TOKEN' }).callback(console.log);
*/
```

- Always give `name`, `summary`, `input` and `output`. `summary` is the description an AI client sees when the action is exposed with `mcp: true`. `output` is also a filter: only the declared keys leave the action.
- Provider options (base URL, token, limits) are in `config` and read as `$.config.<key>`. The default of a secret is an empty string or `YOUR_TOKEN`, never a real value. A caller overrides it with `.config({ ... })`. The base URL belongs in `config` because it lets a test point the action at a local server. Do not read `process.env` inside an action.
- Whatever the provider returns is not trusted: check that the keys you read exist and answer `$.invalid('@(Unknown format)')` instead of crashing. A non-2xx status is not an `err` of `REQUEST`: check `response.status`.
- Reuse other actions with `$.action(...)`: `.callback($)` passes its answer or error on; `await ... .promise($)` gives the value inside an `async` action.
- `route: true`, `user: true`, `permissions`, `timeout` and `mcp: true` only when the task asks for them. Add an `EXAMPLE:` comment at the end showing a call.

## Test

`test.js` runs the action the way an application does, with `ACTION(...)` and the Total.js test library, and asserts the result. A test that only prints is not a test.

```js
require('total5');
require('total5/test');
require('./action');

var FIXTURE = JSON.stringify({ items: [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] });

function call(name, input, config) {
	return ACTION(name, input).env('test').config(config || {}).promise();
}

Test.push('Shipments|parse', async function(next) {

	var out = await call('Shipments|parse', { data: FIXTURE });
	Test.print('returns 2 items', out.items.length === 2 ? null : 'got ' + out.items.length);

	var rejected = false;
	try {
		await call('Shipments|parse', { data: '{}' });
	} catch (e) {
		rejected = true;
	}
	Test.print('rejects an unknown format', rejected ? null : 'did not fail');

	next();
});

Test.run();
```

- `Test.push(name, fn)` registers a step and `fn` calls `next()` when it ends. `Test.print(message)` records `[OK]`; `Test.print(message, error)` with a value records `[FAIL]` and the process exits with code 1. `Test.run()` runs the steps in order and ends the process.
- `.promise()` resolves with the answer and rejects with the error list, for example when a required field is missing.
- Cover for every action: a valid call, a missing required field, an empty or unknown answer of the provider and the edge cases of the data.
- Unit tests do not call the real provider. Use small inline samples or justified fixture files (trimmed, anonymized, without tokens or personal data): passed directly to a `parse` action, or served by a local `Total.Http.createServer` on port `0` and given to the caller through `.config({ url: url })`. Close the server so the test ends by itself.
- Call actions by their explicit name, not `Object.keys(Total.actions)[0]`: the order of files on disk is not a contract.
- `PATH.root(file)` is relative to the folder where `node test.js` runs: run the test from the action's folder.
- An npm dependency of the test is installed with `NPM.wait(NPMINSTALL, function() { ... })`; add one only when it is needed. A live-provider check must be explicitly identified and selected; it does not replace unit tests.

## Checker

`tools/check.js` follows the kit's execution context: new Total.js tools load `total5` and use `Total.*`; an existing plain Node tool may retain its imports (see [definitions and modules](definitions-and-modules.md)). For a folder it checks `node --check`, the `Collection|verb` name, `name`, `summary`, `input`, `output`, that every action answers, that `config` holds no real secret, the ES5 style and `require()` / `process.env` in the action, that the test asserts and uses a local URL, and then runs `test.js`. Run `node tools/check.js actions/<name>` or without arguments for every folder; it ends with the number of errors and the exit code. A passing check does not prove the real provider works: say which part was verified only against a fixture.

## SQL-backed actions and anonymous callers

Use the application's default adapter connection (`DATA.read('tbl_chat')`, for example). Do not prefix every table with `$.config.database` merely to choose a test database. The test initializes the connection; the action remains portable. See [native tests and database setup](../general/testing.md).

Do not add a user/session requirement to a public call-centre or anonymous workflow. Only construct `User` and call `.user(...)` when authentication is part of the action contract. An optional caller name is data, not an authenticated account. Keep audit columns when the schema requires them, leaving them null when no actor exists rather than inventing one.

Document the difference between an omitted optional update field, an explicit empty value and null. A truthiness guard preserves existing values for both omission and empty strings; do not describe it as allowing a clear operation. Specify the allowed values of fixed status fields and whether fields such as channel are unrestricted or enumerated.

## Scope and documentation

Copy the repository's existing example and preserve owner-supplied code. Add only the requested actions and required tests; do not duplicate responsibilities already implemented elsewhere. Tests/configuration/setup helpers are not automatically part of the files copied into an application. Keep setup instructions and test inventories next to the suite that owns them. Respect the repository's lockfile policy; do not introduce package-lock.json into a kit that excludes it.

Document purpose, contract, required setup, commands and actual limits. Omit personal names, conversation history, tool provenance and incidental environment details from deliverables. A comment should explain a necessary decision, not narrate the work.

References: the [native CMS widget tests](https://github.com/totaljs-es/cms-widgets/blob/63892ff/test.js) demonstrate direct Total.js bootstrap and suite config; Framework 5 [test.js](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/7d2d553fc774090081b4e3b1ae75a52ef06b42b8/test.js) defines the runner. SQL connection naming follows the consuming adapter and the existing DATA calls; verify its configured default before changing queries.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/backend/routes-and-auth.md

# Routes and authentication

## Where routes live

In `exports.install` of a file in `controllers/` or of a plugin's `index.js`. One line per route, aligned in columns.

```js
exports.install = function() {

	// Tickets
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets                   --> Tickets|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets_detail/{id}       --> Tickets|read');
	ROUTE('+API    ?       +tickets_create            --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
	ROUTE('+API    ?       +tickets_update/{id}       --> Tickets|update', 1024 * 10);
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets_remove/{id}       --> Tickets|remove');

};
```

Group the lines with a short comment per collection.

## Reading an API route

```
ROUTE('+API    ?    +tickets_create    --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
        |      |     |                     |                |
        |      |     |                     |                max body size in bytes
        |      |     |                     the action
        |      |     "+" the request has a body (input), "-" it has none
        |      the URL of the endpoint; "?" is replaced by CONF.$api ("/api/" by default)
        "+" only for logged-in users; without it the route is public
```

- Endpoint names are lowercase with `_`: `tickets_create`, `users_remove/{id}`. `{id}` fills `$.params.id`.
- Use `-` for reads and removals, `+` for creates and updates.
- A plugin may bind the endpoint to its own base: `ROUTE('+API /setup/ -users --> Users|list')`.
- Without a size, the default body limit applies. Give a limit to routes that take larger bodies.

## Other routes

```js
ROUTE('+GET    /setup/', setup);         // a page, only for logged-in users
ROUTE('POST    /notify/', notify);       // a public route with a handler function
ROUTE('+POST    ?/upload/    @upload <10MB    --> Files|insert');   // an upload: @upload for multipart, <10MB for the size
```

A handler function is `function($)`. Prefer an API route plus an action; use a plain handler for pages, files and webhooks.

## A route declared in the action

`NEWACTION` also accepts `route: '+API ?'` (or `route: true`) and registers the endpoint itself. It is not restricted to small apps; explicit controller or plugin routes are equally valid. Follow one registration style for the feature; do not add a duplicate explicit route for an action that already registers its own.

`route: true` builds an API route, adding authentication when `user` or `permissions` requires it. An explicit route string controls its own prefix; inspect it rather than assuming all `route:` forms imply authentication. Automatic endpoint names come from action IDs. Preserve their spelling in `tapi()` calls.

## Authentication

One `AUTH` in `definitions/auth.js`. It decides who the request is and calls `$.success(user)` or `$.invalid()`.

```js
AUTH(function($) {
	var token = $.headers['x-token'];
	if (token) {
		if (BLOCKED($, 10)) {      // too many wrong tries from this client
			$.invalid();
			return;
		}
		if (token === CONF.token) {
			BLOCKED($, -1);        // forget the failures
			$.success(BOT);
		} else
			$.invalid();
	} else
		$.invalid();
});
```

- The user object is small: `{ id, name, sa, permissions }`. `sa` marks a super administrator.
- Use `BLOCKED($, limit)` to rate-limit failed logins: it counts tries per `$.ip` and returns `true` once the limit is passed (`BLOCKED($, -1)` clears the count). Because it keys on `$.ip`, it inherits the `X-Forwarded-For` caveat below.
- `+` routes require authentication; action-level checks apply when configured. Test authenticated, anonymous and insufficient-permission requests.
- `$.ip` takes the first value of `X-Forwarded-For`, which a client can forge. For security limits use `$.req.socket.remoteAddress`, or trust the header only behind your own proxy.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/backend/definitions-and-modules.md

# Definitions and modules

## definitions/

Files here are loaded when the app starts. They export nothing: they register things on the framework. One file per concern.

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `auth.js` | the single `AUTH(...)` |
| `init.js` | config defaults and `ON('ready', ...)`: load caches, register UI components |
| `func.js` | shared helpers as `FUNC.name = function() {}` |
| `db.js` | shared state objects (`MAIN.id`, `MAIN.db`) |

```js
// definitions/init.js
CONF.version = '1';
if (!CONF.cdn)
	CONF.cdn = 'https://cdn.componentator.com';

ON('ready', function() {
	setTimeout(FUNC.load, 500);
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,form,validate,...', true);
});
```

```js
// definitions/func.js
FUNC.refreshtags = async function() {
	REPO.tags = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').promise();
};
```

- Helpers are named in lowercase without separators: `FUNC.refreshtags`, `FUNC.notify`.
- Use `ON('ready')` for anything that needs the app and the database to be up.
- `EMIT('configure')` / `ON('configure')` is how parts of the app react to a config change.

## config

A plain file, one `key : value` per line. Read it with `CONF.key`. Settings the framework owns start with `$`: `$api`, `$minifyjs`. Secrets (keys, database URLs) do not belong in a repository: keep them in the deployment config.

## modules/

A module is an integration with another system or a self-contained service (`cdn.js`, `visitors.js`). Total.js loads `modules/*.js` automatically and registers the exports under `MODS`, using `exports.id` or the filename without its extension. The loader calls `exports.install()` when that method exists; a module exposing reusable methods does not need an empty installer.

Use that registry from initialized application code. Example:

```js
var data = MODS.visitors.today();
var visitors = MODS.visitors.instance.visitors;
```

Hyphenated IDs use bracket access, for example `MODS['knowledge-source']`. Do not repeatedly import an application module with `require(PATH.root('modules/...'))`. Name application modules `.js`; a `.cjs` helper is not automatically registered by the `modules` scan.

`MODS` exists after framework initialization, but an entry exists only after its module loads. Read another module from an exported method or an appropriate lifecycle callback; do not depend on sibling filename order or introduce circular initialization. Work needing application state or a database belongs in the existing ready/configure lifecycle. An automatically called `install()` must not require arguments supplied only by a later controller.

A standalone Node tool does not acquire loaded application modules merely by requiring `total5`. It may import a shared CommonJS helper directly. Preserve that execution boundary when code is shared with validators or maintenance tools; do not replace valid CLI imports with an unpopulated `MODS` entry. The `total5` bootstrap and third-party database adapters also retain their required imports.

Keep a module independent: it reads `CONF`, not another integration's private internals. Some integrations expose a dedicated global; preserve that public contract when present. New application module consumers use `MODS`.

## Shared state

- `MAIN`: the application's own state (`MAIN.db`, `MAIN.cache`).
- `REPO`: cached lookups that the UI also needs (`REPO.tags`, `REPO.ui`).
- `FUNC`: functions shared by actions and controllers.
- `MODS`: automatically registered application module exports.

Do not create new globals. Hang things from these three.

## Config in the database

When settings live in a table (`cl_config`), load them with `LOADCONFIG(rows)` and emit `configure`, as a `FUNC.reconfigure` does.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/backend/storage-and-integrations.md

# Storage and integrations

Choose the model already used by the feature. Not every app stores data in SQL.

## Persistence and cache ownership

| Model | How to extend it |
|---|---|
| Metadata in memory, serialized to FileStorage | Mutate the existing collection, call `FUNC.save()`, refresh affected rendering caches when necessary |
| SQL through `DATA` and `querybuilderpg` | Keep projections, filters, identifiers, response shapes and adapter initialization |
| Named persisted memory object | Keep `MEMORIZE` object ownership and existing save hooks |
| Flow state | Keep flow load/save lifecycle and websocket permissions together |

Do not switch models during a cleanup.

A `FUNC.load` typically reads the metadata, initializes defaults, compiles derived objects and emits reload; `FUNC.save` excludes compiled references before serialization. Changing a record can therefore require cache refresh as well as saving. Follow the feature's actual invalidation path rather than inventing a second cache.

## A new application: which storage

An existing feature keeps its model. A new application chooses by what the data is:

| The data | Use |
|---|---|
| The records of the application (contacts, tasks, orders), small today and maybe on PostgreSQL tomorrow | `DATA` with QueryBuilder from the start: `DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact')` on the embedded NoSQL database |
| An embedded store that will never be SQL (a log, a queue, a cache on disk) | `NOSQL('name')` directly |
| A small named object that is kept by itself (settings, counters) | `MEMORIZE('name')` |
| Files and their metadata | `FILESTORAGE('name')` |

`DATA` works on the embedded NoSQL database with the prefix `nosql/` before the name of the table. It needs no definition and no dependency:

```js
var items = await DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);
var item = await DATA.read('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
await DATA.insert('nosql/tbl_contact', model).promise($);
await DATA.modify('nosql/tbl_contact', model).id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
await DATA.remove('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
```

The file is `databases/tbl_contact.nosql`, the same one that `NOSQL('tbl_contact')` reads. Name the tables and the columns as in SQL from the start (`tbl_contact`, `isdone`, `dtcreated`; see [SQL scripts](../database/sql-scripts.md)).

An application written this way moves to PostgreSQL without writing its queries again: it adds the definition of its adapter and takes the prefix `nosql/` away from the table names.

```js
// definitions/db.js
require('querybuilderpg').init('default', CONF.database, 1, ERROR('PostgreSQL'));
```

```js
var items = await DATA.find('tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);
```

The prefix is the form of the framework's own tests and of the CMS (`DATA.modify('nosql/pages', ...)`). Checked with Total.js 5 0.0.19: `apps/contacts` (embedded database) and `apps/contacts-postgresql` (PostgreSQL 18) of the [knowledge repository](https://github.com/totaljs-es/knowledge) have the same queries and pass the same tests.

## Outgoing requests

Use `RESTBuilder` and the existing integration configuration. A notification that is intentionally independent can use `RESTBuilder.POST(...).callback(NOOP)`; use explicit error handling when an action's result depends on the remote call.

Illustrative request-dependent pattern (adapted to the request style in the framework's `builders.js`, `RESTP.promise`):

```js
var response = await RESTBuilder.GET(CONF.serviceurl).promise($);
```

Check the remote status and response shape required by the integration before returning success. Do not assume a network-success callback proves a valid business response. In a job without `$`, use an error-first callback or handle `.promise()` rejection. Reuse project timeouts, authentication and cancellation conventions when present; verify support in the installed version.

## Configuration and lifecycle

Read configuration through `CONF` and follow the target app's settings loader. Use `LOADCONFIG` and `configure` hooks; service listeners refresh or reload state periodically. Do not add a parallel environment/config system to a feature that already has settings.

- Startup work belongs in the existing ready/init path.
- React to configuration changes through the existing `ON('configure', ...)` / `EMIT('configure')` flow.
- Repeated maintenance uses the app's `ON('service', function(counter) { ... })` convention where available, rather than one timer per action call.
- Keep request-dependent errors observable. Use `ERROR('context')` where the surrounding app expects a logging callback; use `NOOP` only for deliberately ignored results.

Do not copy development credentials or permissive demo auth into a new deployment.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/backend/gotchas.md

# Gotchas of the server

Things that behave differently from what you would guess. Each one is a rule.

## Answers

- In an **action**, `$.callback(data)` returns data. In a plain **route handler** (`function($)`), `$.callback(err, value)` takes the error first: answer with `$.json(data)` instead.
- `$.invalid(404)`: a number above 399 sets the HTTP status (an omitted error becomes 401 in `ErrorBuilder.push`; use an explicit code for clarity). `$.invalid('@(text)')` answers with the message; its second argument is the `path` of the field the error belongs to, not a status code.
- On a handler you can also set the status yourself: `$.response.status = 401; $.json(...)`.

## Request data

- Route parameters (`{id}`) are in `$.params`.
- In a controller, `$.body` is parsed and `$.payload` holds the buffered raw body for the supported body-parsing path. In an action, `$.payload` / `model` is the action input, not that raw HTTP buffer. For webhook signatures use the controller context and verify the route flags/content type preserve the bytes you sign.
- `$.ip` is the first `X-Forwarded-For` value: forgeable. Use `$.req.socket.remoteAddress` for security limits.
- When changing CSRF handling, check `Controller.prototype.csrf` and view directive support; verify token generation and validation together. Do not introduce an alternative transport solely because a past app needed one.
- Session checks depend on the app's authentication module. Inspect its cookie, token and user-agent checks before assuming a session is portable between clients.

## Schemas and input

- A `Boolean` that is absent is `false`. Use `partial: true` when absence must mean "unchanged".
- With `partial`, a `null` number is ignored; use `0` for "none".
- `*field:[String]` rejects an empty list; drop the `*` if empty is allowed.
- Never `for...in` over an array. Use a classic `for` loop.

## Served JavaScript and static files

- `node --check` does not validate the release minifier or browser execution. Check the served asset when changing regular expressions or template syntax. Diagnose a reproducible failure before disabling `$minifyjs`; do not make a global configuration change as a style fix.
- In release, static files are served from memory: restart the app after changing them. Browsers also cache: force a reload while testing.

## Data

- NoSQL: `NOSQL('x').find().where(...)`; `.sort(field, true)` is **descending**. Updates append a line and mark the old one, so the file grows until it is cleaned.
- NoSQL dates arrive on the server as `Date`, on the client as text.

## Tests

- `opt.config` passed to `Total.run` is overridden by `(env)` entries of the config: set `process.env` first.
- Before running a translation extractor, check its scan scope and keep generated/vendor directories out of the input. Verify the resulting `.resource` files.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/database/sql-scripts.md

# SQL scripts (PostgreSQL)

## Files

- `database.sql` holds the whole current schema, so a new installation needs one file.
- Preserve the existing root SQL-file layout in apps that use it. When grouping SQL and maintenance files in a directory, use `private/database/`; update application readers, migration tools and package allowlists together. This layout policy does not change the SQL contract. See [project structure](../general/project-structure.md).
- A change to an existing installation goes in a separate script next to it, named with a date: `database-2024-10-30.sql`. Prefer the dated name with dashes, as the file rule requires.
- The first lines of an upgrade script say which version it upgrades from and that it must run before the app starts.
- Inside a script, order the objects: **tables, views, functions and stored procedures, indexes**, each part under a banner comment (`-- TABLES`, `-- VIEWS`, `-- INDEXES`).
- Wrap the script in `BEGIN; ... COMMIT;` so that it applies completely or not at all.

## Names

All lowercase, singular.

| Object | Prefix | Example |
|---|---|---|
| table | `tbl_` | `tbl_user`, `tbl_ticket_time` |
| code list (rarely changes, used for choices) | `cl_` | `cl_status`, `cl_type` |
| view | `view_` | `view_ticket` |
| stored procedure | `sp_` | `sp_user` |
| function | `fn_` | `fn_user` |

Name indexes `<table>_idx<what>`: `tbl_ticket_idxstatus`. Name foreign keys `<table>_<column>_fkey`.

## Columns

- Type `text`, not `varchar`. Lists are `_text`, structured data `json` or `jsonb`, small numbers `int2`, dates `timestamp`, flags `bool`.
- `id` is the primary key, `text`, filled in the code with `UID()`. A foreign key is the table plus `id`: `userid`, `folderid`, `parentid`.
- Dates start with `dt`: `dtcreated`, `dtupdated`, `dtremoved`. Booleans start with `is`: `isremoved`, `ispublic`, `isdisabled`.
- Use the same names for the same thing in every table: `name`, `body`, `search`, `sortindex`, `icon`, `color`.
- New feature tables include `id`, `name` and `dtcreated`. Preserve established schemas and externally owned contracts; document a concrete exception instead of treating these columns as optional by default.
- Tables tracking changes normally also have `createdby`, `updatedby`, `removedby` as `jsonb`, and `dtupdated`, `dtremoved`. Without an authenticated actor, keep the author columns nullable rather than fabricating a user. A caller display field such as `username` is separate from authorship.
- `dtcreated` defaults to UTC now: `DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now())`.
- A column that lists search keywords is called `search`.

## Order of the columns

Identifiers first, then main fields, numbers, booleans, and dates last. Then the constraints and the primary key.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "public"."tbl_ticket" (
	"id" text NOT NULL,
	"folderid" text,
	"ownerid" text,
	"name" text,
	"search" text,
	"attrs" json,
	"worked" int4 DEFAULT 0,
	"ispublic" bool DEFAULT false,
	"isremoved" bool DEFAULT false,
	"dtupdated" timestamp,
	"dtcreated" timestamp DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now()),
	CONSTRAINT "tbl_ticket_folderid_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("folderid") REFERENCES "public"."tbl_folder"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
	PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);
```

## Code lists

A `cl_` table holds the choices of the app and is read once into memory.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "public"."cl_status" (
	"id" text NOT NULL,
	"name" text,
	"icon" text,
	"color" text,
	"sortindex" int2 DEFAULT 0,
	PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);
```

## Format

Tabs (width 4), no useless casts (`name <> 'x'`, not `name <> 'x'::text`), one statement per `;`, a trailing `;` on every command.

## Audit fields and migrations

Authorship fields are project schema conventions, not automatically populated database/framework columns. For a feature that records changes, include the columns and leave the actor null when no authenticated identity exists:

```sql
"createdby" jsonb,
"updatedby" jsonb,
"removedby" jsonb,
"dtcreated" timestamp DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now()),
"dtupdated" timestamp,
"dtremoved" timestamp
```

Optional display fields such as username or summary belong only to features that need them. A schema default is not a migration of existing tables: add an upgrade when introducing columns or renaming tables in an installed application.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/database/queries.md

# Queries with `DATA`

For SQL-backed features, Total.js uses `DATA` and the configured database adapter (for example `querybuilderpg`). Do not introduce SQL into a FileStorage/MEMORIZE feature just to match this page. Use the builder for what it can express; write raw SQL only when needed.

For request-bound results use `.promise($)` (in an async action), `.callback($)` or `.callback($.done(id))`. In jobs and shared helpers without a request use `.promise()` with explicit error handling or an error-first callback. Do not invent a request context. Some source apps enqueue background writes without awaiting them; do not copy that when the response depends on the write succeeding.

## Read

```js
// one record
var item = await DATA.read('tbl_user').fields('id,name').id(params.id).error('@(User not found)').promise($);

// several
var items = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').where('folderid', id).promise($);

// values from a list
var apps = await DATA.find('op.tbl_app_permission').fields('id,appid').in('id', permissions).promise($);
```

- `.fields('a,b')` selects columns; name them, do not read `*`.
- `.id(value)` filters by the primary key.
- `.error('@(text)')` or `.error(404)` answers with that error when nothing is found. It is what turns a missing row into a 404.

## A list for the UI

`autoquery` reads the query string (`?q=`, `sort`, `page`, `limit`) and builds the query. Name the allowed fields and their types, a default sort and a maximum page size:

```js
NEWACTION('Groups|list', {
	name: 'List of groups',
	action: function($) {
		DATA.find('op.view_group').autoquery($.query, 'id:UID,name,color,icon,users:Number,dtcreated:Date,dtupdated:Date', 'dtcreated_desc', 100).callback($);
	}
});
```
