A reusable joined list often reads from a `view_`. `DATA.list(...)` is used for paginated output and `DATA.find(...)` for plain lists. Preserve the response shape expected by the UI rather than swapping them because their query chains look similar.

## Write

```js
model.id = UID();
model.dtcreated = NOW;
await DATA.insert('tbl_ticket_time', model).promise($);

model.dtupdated = NOW;
await DATA.modify('op.tbl_group', model).id(params.id).error('@(Group not found)').promise($);

await DATA.remove('tbl_tag').id(params.id).error(404).promise($);
await DATA.remove('tbl_notification').where('ticketid', params.id).where('typeid', 'logwork').promise($);
```

- Fill `id` with `UID()` and the dates with `NOW` in the action, not in the database.
- Remove fields that are not columns before `insert` / `modify` (`model.permissions = undefined`).
- Update or insert in one call: `DATA.modify('tbl_x', data, true).id(id).insert(fn, params)`.

## Success after a write

When a write should return the app's success envelope rather than its raw database result, use:

```js
DATA.remove('tbl_tag').id($.params.id).error(404).callback($.done($.params.id));
```

Keep the established response contract. A raw `.callback($)` and `$.done(id)` are not interchangeable responses.

## Conditions

`where(field, value)`, `in(field, array)`, `notin(field, array)`, `search(field, keyword)`, `or(function(b) { b.search('name', m); b.search('email', m); })`.

```js
var keywords = text.toKeywords(true, true);
for (var i = 0; i < keywords.length; i++)
	builder.search('a.search', keywords[i]);
```

## Raw SQL

`DATA.query('UPDATE tbl_ticket a SET worked=(SELECT ...) WHERE a.id=$1', [id]).promise($)`.

- Prefer parameters (`$1`) over building the text.
- When a value must go into the text, escape it with `PG_ESCAPE(value)` before `.format()`. Never concatenate user input.

## Schemas (namespaces)

A table can be addressed with its schema: `op.tbl_user`. Keep the prefix consistent inside one file.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/components.md

# Components (jComponent)

For widgets, forms, lists, inputs and every other piece of UI, **use a component that already exists**. If none fits, **create a component** (do not build the piece with ad hoc markup and scripts). Load catalogue components with `COMPONENTATOR()`; custom app-owned components remain normal app assets.

## 1. Look for the component first

The catalogue of jComponent components, with a live preview, the documentation and the download of each, is Componentator: <https://componentator.com>.

Before writing UI:

1. Find the component that does the job (input, form, listing, datagrid, notify, menu, approve...).
2. Read its page: what it does, its **configuration** and its context (what path and data it expects, what it needs around it).
3. Use it from markup with `<ui-component name="..." path="..." config="...">`.

Machine-readable forms of the same catalogue (use these from code or an agent):

| What | URL |
|---|---|
| The index for models: rules, the reference component and the API of the library | `https://componentator.com/llms.txt` |
| One component as markdown | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs/components/master/components/<name>/readme.md` (e.g. `input`, lowercase) |
| The source of one component, with its live example | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs/components/master/components/<name>/component.html` |

The readme of each component says the versions of jComponent it works with (`jcomponent: v19,v20`).

## Match the UI version first

Apps load `spa.min@19` or `@20`. A catalogue entry for jComponent 20 does not prove its markup or options work in 19. Check the actual layout, bundle and nearby screen before using a component or copying `PLUGIN`/binding syntax. A backend Total.js 5 dependency does not select the browser UI major version.

## Preferred components

When several components could do the job, use these:

| For | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Form fields (text, email, phone, password, multiline, checkbox, select, date...) | `input` (j-Input) | One component for every field: `type` chooses the kind. It replaces j-Textbox and j-Dropdown. |
| A box with a fixed height and scroll | `viewbox` | `height` is a percentage, `parent` is the container (or `window`), `scroll` / `scrollbar` control scrolling. |
| Loaders | `loading` | Reacts to the `@showloading` and `@hideloading` flags; `style` picks the look (1 = spinner, 2 = line at the top). |
| Tables and data grids | `datagrid` | For single page and enterprise apps: filters, sorting, pages, `height` modes (`auto`, `fluid`, `parent`). |
| Buttons and calls to functions | `exec` | See below. |
| Predefined design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode) | `intranetcss` | Ready-made CSS classes; see below. |

### exec: buttons and function calls

`exec` is a singleton that works for the whole page: any element with the class `exec` calls a function when it is clicked. Do not add `onclick` handlers or `addEventListener` for buttons.

```html
<button class="exec" data-exec="?/create"><i class="ti ti-plus-circle"></i>@(Create)</button>
<span class="exec" data-exec="?/options" data-prevent="true">...</span>
<a class="exec" data-href="/offers/">@(Offers)</a>
```

- `data-exec="NAME"`: the function to call, with the form `function(element, event)`. A `?` calls a method of the current plugin (`?/create` is `exports.create`).
- `data-prevent="true"`: stops the click from going further (for a button inside a clickable row).
- `data-href="URL"`: redirects instead of calling a function.
- Double click and context menu use the same attributes with a suffix: `data-exec2` (class `exec2`) and `data-exec3` (class `exec3`).

### intranetcss: predefined design

`intranetcss` is a component made only of CSS. It brings the shared look of the intranet apps, with a dark mode, so a screen does not need its own style for the common pieces:

- containers: `.panel` (with `label` and `.toolbar`), `.padding`, `.divider`, `.bg-smoke`
- lists and menus: `.listing`, `.listing2`, `.nav`, `.tabmenu`, `.tabmenu2`, `.iconmenu`, `.keyvalue`
- messages and badges: `.message`, `.message-success`, `.message-error`, `.message-alert`, `.badge` (with colors and sizes)
- sizes: `.small`, `.medium`, `.large`

Use these classes before writing new CSS (see [css](css.md)). Its source (version 5) is served by the component download service.

## 2. If it does not exist, create a component

A piece of UI that has behaviour is a component, not a block of script inside a page.

```js
COMPONENT('name', function(self, config, cls) {
	// keep the names: "self", "config" and "cls"
});
```

- Names of components, plugins, variables and settings in **lowercase**.
- Keep at most 2-3 levels of nesting in objects.
- Avoid `_` in variable names.
- **Think reusable**: a component takes its data from `path` and its options from `config`, and knows nothing about the screen that uses it.
- Use the same name across projects for the same thing. Check the catalogue before choosing one.

## 3. Load components with COMPONENTATOR()

For shared catalogue components, use the app's `COMPONENTATOR()` bundle. App-owned components load through the app's existing assets. For example, in `definitions/init.js`:

```js
ON('ready', function() {
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,page,viewbox,input,form,validate,loading,datagrid,intranetcss,message,menu,approve,notify,errorhandler', true);
});
```

`COMPONENTATOR(name, components, removeprev, attrs)`:

- `name`: the name of the bundle (`'ui'`).
- `components`: the components of the bundle, comma-separated, without the `j-` prefix.
- `removeprev` (default `true`): deletes the older bundles of the same name when the list changes.
- `attrs`: optional extra parameters for the bundle.

The framework downloads the bundle once, saves it in `public/` as `ui-<name>-<hash>.min.js` and stores its address in `REPO.<name>`. The layout loads it:

```html
<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
```

Rules:

- One `COMPONENTATOR()` call per bundle (`ui` for the app, `webui` for public pages).
- List **only** the components the app uses: the bundle is what every user downloads.
- When you start using a component, add it to the list; when no screen uses it any more, remove it.
- A component you created yourself is a normal file of the app (`public/` or the plugin's `public/`), not a `COMPONENTATOR()` entry.

## Adapt the official component's appearance

Reuse the official component and its configuration first. A different visual design usually needs a scoped CSS skin, not a copied component implementation or a file that embeds jComponent itself.

The official `backtotop` is loaded through `COMPONENTATOR('webui', 'backtotop', true)` and declared as:

```html
<ui-component name="backtotop" class="app-backtotop" config="icon:ti ti-arrow-up;$init:FUNC.backtotop" data-label="@(Back to top)"></ui-component>
```

A stylesheet changes the appearance; a `FUNC` function adds button semantics, a translated accessible name and keyboard focus handling through the native `$init` hook. The official component retains its scrolling and visibility behavior. The hook is needed because the official component renders a span; CSS cannot provide button semantics.

Verify hook timing against the installed runtime and component: jComponent's `library.js` calls `make` before applying `$init`, so the hook can adapt the generated markup. Keep such hooks small and idempotent, and check Enter, Space, pointer interaction, focus and reduced motion. If a component supplies the required semantics already, use them directly.

## 4. Quick check

- Is there a component for this in the catalogue? Use it.
- Did you read its configuration and context before using it? Do.
- Is it in the `COMPONENTATOR()` list? Add it.
- Is there none? Create a reusable `COMPONENT('name', ...)` and use it from markup.

See [plugins-ui](plugins-ui.md) for how screens and forms use components, and [views-and-layout](views-and-layout.md) for the layout that loads the bundle.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/plugins-ui.md

# Plugins with UI

A feature of an app is a **plugin**: a folder with a server part and a UI part that the framework loads and the app shell mounts.

```
plugins/redirects/
	index.js              server: metadata + routes
	schemas/redirects.js  actions (see backend/actions.md)
	public/index.html     the screen: markup + <script>PLUGIN(...)</script>
	public/form.html      the form that opens over the screen
```

## Server part: index.js

```js
exports.icon = 'ti ti-exchange';
exports.name = '@(Redirects)';
exports.position = 3;
exports.permissions = [{ id: 'redirects', name: 'Redirects' }];
exports.visible = function(user) {
	return user.sa || user.permissions.indexOf('redirects') !== -1 || user.permissions.indexOf('admin') !== -1;
};

exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -redirects_list               --> Redirects|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +redirects_save               --> Redirects|save');
};
```

- `icon` is a Total Icons class (`ti ti-name`), `name` is translatable with `@(...)`, `position` orders the menu.
- `permissions` declares what the plugin adds; `visible` decides who sees it.
- Routes use the same syntax as everywhere (see [routes-and-auth](../backend/routes-and-auth.md)).

## UI part: a screen

A screen is HTML with a `<ui-plugin>` root and one `PLUGIN(function(exports) { ... })` block. Keep markup, scoped style and logic in the same file. Screens may also include a `virtualwire` toolbar, importer declarations and other app-shell wrappers; copy the nearest screen rather than enforcing exactly one root element.

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
</style>

<ui-plugin class="CLASS bg-white">
	<ui-component name="empty" path="?.items" config="parent:auto" class="invisible">
		...
	</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		exports.reload = function() {
			exports.refresh();
		};

		exports.refresh = function() {
			exports.tapi('redirects_list', function(response) {
				exports.set('items', response);
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

Rules:

- `CLASS` in selectors and class lists is replaced with a unique class for the plugin: it scopes the CSS so plugins do not collide.
- `?` in a path (`?.items`, `?/create`) means "this plugin": `?.items` is the data, `?/create` is `exports.create`.
- `exports.reload` runs every time the screen opens.
- Call the server with `exports.tapi('endpoint_name', data, callback)`. Add `ERROR` after the name (`'redirects_read ERROR'`) to show an error message to the user automatically.
- Set data with `exports.set('items', value)`, or globally with `SET('path @reset', value)`; read the model with `exports.model`.
- Handlers are attached in markup: `class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}"`. Read the attribute with `ATTRD(el)`.
- Text for people is always `@(Text)` so it can be translated.
- Naming: plugin, component and global names in **lowercase**; keep the names `exports`, `self`, `config`, `cls` as they are.

Official guide on names:

```js
// BAD
PLUGIN('Name', function(plugin) { plugin.doSomething = function() {}; });

// GOOD
PLUGIN('name', function(exports) { exports.dosomething = function() {}; });
```

See [binding and forms](binding-and-forms.md) for the importer, model path, submit callback and caller refresh as one connected flow.

## A form

A form is a second file loaded with an `importer` and shown by `miniform` / `form`. It has `?.field` inputs, a `validate` that enables the submit button, and a `submit` function.

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;icon:ti ti-exchange;autofocus:true;reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<div class="m">
			<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1;placeholder:@(Relative URL address)">@(URL)</ui-component>
		</div>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled><i class="ti ti-check-circle"></i>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>
```

Open it from the screen:

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
	SET('*form', 'formredirect');
};
```

## Confirm and menu

```js
SETTER('approve/show', '@(Are you sure you want to remove it?)', ':ti ti-trash: @(Remove)', function() {
	exports.tapi('redirects_remove/ ERROR', { id: id }, function() { exports.refresh(); });
});
SETTER('menu/show', opt);
```

## Think reusable

Components, plugins and global names are shared across projects. Before inventing one, look in the [catalogue of components](components.md) and in another app for the same name.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/views-and-layout.md

# Views and layout

## Layout

The shell of an app is one HTML file in `views/` (`admin.html`, `index.html`). It sets the title, loads the UI library, registers global components once and mounts the plugins.

```html
@{layout('')}
@{title(config.name)}

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<meta charset="utf-8" />
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
	<link href="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.css" rel="stylesheet" />
	<script src="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js"></script>
	<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
	@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.js + func.js', 'default.css', 'favicon.ico')}
</head>
<body class="invisible">

	<ui-component name="exec"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="errorhandler"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="locale" config="requests:1;language:@{language}"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="LAZY menu" config="style:2"></ui-component>

</body>
</html>
```

- Directives start with `@{...}`: `@{title()}`, `@{import()}`, `@{if}` / `@{fi}`, `@{REPO.ui}`, `https://cdn.componentator.com` (a config value).
- Global components are declared once in the layout. `LAZY` loads a component only when it is first used.
- The component bundle is loaded with `COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,...', true)` in `definitions/init.js`. List only the components the app uses; see [components](components.md).
- `<body class="invisible">` hides the page until the UI is ready.

## Runtime, bundles and application assets

New layouts load jComponent 20 from the CDN. An existing app on another major version requires a deliberate migration.

- Load `https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.css` and `https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js` once per document. The runtime must precede component bundles and scripts that use its APIs.
- `COMPONENTATOR()` downloads the selected components; it does not replace the core runtime. Load the matching `@{REPO.ui}` or `@{REPO.webui}` after the runtime.
- Keep application helpers in app assets, such as `public/js/func.js`, and preserve the existing browser `FUNC` object when extending it. Load helpers before components that call them during initialization.
- Keep the app stylesheet and scoped component skins after the base stylesheet; see [CSS](css.md). Remove embedded copies of the runtime and obsolete custom loaders when adopting this setup.
- An isolated recipe iframe can intentionally use a pinned runtime with its own hashes and evidence. It is a separate document; preserve that version boundary.

Changing asset loading must preserve the existing title, language, canonical and alternate URLs, metadata, structured data, agent discovery links, landmarks and accessible navigation. Check the rendered HTML and browser console, keyboard interaction, mobile layout and reduced-motion behavior. A component initializing successfully does not establish that the whole layout is accessible.

## Translations

Every text a person reads is wrapped in `@(...)`, in views, in plugin HTML and in server messages: `@(Save)`. The text in English is the key.

## Two kinds of pages

- **App screens** (admin, tools): plugin HTML mounted in the layout, driven by `PLUGIN`.
- **Public pages**: server-rendered views returned by a controller (`$.view('index')`). They carry no `PLUGIN` logic.

## Naming

Lowercase file names with `-`: `search-results.html`, `form-offer.html`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/tangular.md

# Tangular templates

Tangular is the template engine of Total.js: text with `{{ ... }}` commands that is filled with a model. jComponent uses it in the browser for everything a screen draws from data, and the framework has the same engine on the server.

Every example of this page was run with the engine of Total.js 5 0.0.19; the result is after `=>`.

## Where it is used

In a screen, a `ui-bind` with `config="template"` draws its `<script type="text/html">` every time its path changes. Inside the template the data of the path is `value`:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.items" config="template" class="block">
	<script type="text/html">
		{{ foreach m in value }}
		<div class="item{{ if m.isdone }} done{{ fi }}">{{ m.name }}</div>
		{{ end }}
	</script>
</ui-bind>
```

On the server, and anywhere in JavaScript:

```js
var html = Tangular.render('Hello {{ name }}!', { name: 'Anna' });   // => Hello Anna!

var template = Tangular.compile('Hello {{ name }}!');                 // a function, to render many times
var html2 = template({ name: 'Zoe' });                                // => Hello Zoe!
```

Tangular is not the syntax of the views: a view of `views/` uses `@{...}` (see [views and layout](views-and-layout.md)). `{{ ... }}` is for templates.

## Values

| Template | Model | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `{{ name }}` | `{ name: 'Anna <b>' }` | `Anna &lt;b&gt;` |
| `{{ html \| raw }}` | `{ html: '<b>bold</b>' }` | `<b>bold</b>` |
| `{{ user.name }}` | `{ user: { name: 'Anna' } }` | `Anna` |
| `{{ age + 1 }}` | `{ age: 31 }` | `32` |
| `{{ nothing }}` | `{ nothing: null }` | an empty text |

- A value is HTML-encoded: text of a user can be shown as it is.
- `| raw` writes the value without encoding. Use it only for HTML that the application made itself.
- `{{ !html }}` is not raw: `!` is the negation of JavaScript, and the result is `false`.
- A value that is `null` or does not exist is an empty text, not an error.

## Conditions

```html
{{ if isadmin }}admin{{ else }}user{{ fi }}
{{ if age > 40 }}old{{ else if age > 30 }}middle{{ else }}young{{ fi }}
{{ if isadmin && age > 18 }}yes{{ fi }}
```

A condition is a JavaScript expression. It ends with `{{ fi }}`.

## Loops

```html
{{ foreach m in items }}[{{ m.name }}]{{ end }}                       => [Bread][Cake]
{{ foreach m in items }}{{ $index }}:{{ m.name }} {{ end }}           => 0:Bread 1:Cake
{{ foreach m in items }}{{ m.name }}{{ if $index < items.length - 1 }}, {{ fi }}{{ end }}   => Bread, Cake
```

- A loop ends with `{{ end }}`. A condition ends with `{{ fi }}`: they are not the same word.
- `$index` is the position of the item, from 0.
- `{{ continue }}` goes to the next item and `{{ break }}` ends the loop.

```html
{{ foreach m in items }}{{ if !m.isdone }}{{ continue }}{{ fi }}{{ m.name }}{{ end }}
```

## Helpers

A helper changes a value: `{{ value | helper }}` or `{{ value | helper(arguments) }}`.

| Template | Value | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `{{ price \| format(2) }}` | `1234.5` | `1 234.50` |
| `{{ date \| format('yyyy-MM-dd') }}` | a date | `2026-11-12` |
| `{{ date \| format('dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm') }}` | a date | `12.11.2026 09:30` |
| `{{ name \| empty('No name') }}` | `''` | `No name` |
| `{{ name \| empty }}` | `''` | `---` |
| `{{ nothing \| def('nothing here') }}` | `null` | `nothing here` |
| `{{ count \| pluralize('no items', '# item', '# items', '# items') }}` | `0`, `3` | `no items`, `3 items` |
| `{{ html \| raw }}` | `<b>bold</b>` | `<b>bold</b>` |

`format` uses the `format` of the value: decimals for a number, a pattern for a date. `empty` and `def` give a text when there is no value. The four texts of `pluralize` are for zero, one, a few and many, and `#` is the number.

## Your own helper

```js
Thelpers.upper = function(value) {
	return Thelpers.encode((value || '').toUpperCase());
};
```

```html
{{ name | upper }}
```

`Tangular.register('upper', fn)` does the same. The result of a helper is written as it is, without encoding: a helper that returns text of a user encodes it with `Thelpers.encode(value)`, as the one above. A helper is the place for what a template repeats (a badge, a status, a size of a file), not a function that builds HTML in the code of the screen.

## What to avoid

- Building HTML with text concatenation or with DOM calls when a template can draw it: change the model and let the `ui-bind` draw.
- `| raw` on text that a user wrote.
- `{{ end }}` to close a condition, or `{{ fi }}` to close a loop.
- `@{...}` inside a template, or `{{ ... }}` in a view of the server, expecting the other engine.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/binding-and-forms.md

# Binding and forms as one flow

The following connected example includes only the fields needed to show the lifecycle. It assumes the app shell, jComponent version, importer and `*form` alias setup; it is not a standalone page.

## Screen → model → importer

The screen declares the form importer and opens a model with the same name. The app's importer replaces `CLASS` when loading the form.

```html
<ui-component name="importer" path="common.form" config="if:formredirect;url:/~ID~/form.html"></ui-component>
```

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
	SET('*form', 'formredirect');
};

exports.edit = function(el) {
	var id = ATTRD(el);
	exports.tapi('redirects_read ERROR', { id: id }, function(response) {
		SET('formredirect @reset', response);
		SET('*form', 'formredirect');
	});
};
```

`formredirect`, the form's `CLASS`, the importer condition, `common.form` and `*form` must agree with the target shell. Do not copy the open function into another app without its alias/importer setup. Read data before showing an edit form; initialize a new model before showing create so the previous record does not leak into it.

## Form → submit → caller refresh

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;title:@(Redirect);reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1">@(URL)</ui-component>
		<ui-component name="input" path="?.target" config="required:1">@(Target URL)</ui-component>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		var caller;

		exports.reload = function() {
			caller = exports.caller;
		};

		exports.submit = function(hide) {
			var model = exports.form;
			exports.tapi('redirects_save ERROR', model, function() {
				hide();
				caller.exec('refresh');
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

The form component owns the submit/cancel buttons. Ordinary screen buttons use `exec`; do not add a second submit listener. Hide only after a successful response, then refresh the caller. Verify `exports.form` / `exports.model` against the actual UI version and nearby form; they are not names to exchange mechanically.

## Binding and templates

Screens bind `?.items` through `ui-bind` and render a `script type="text/html"` with Tangular. Update the model (`exports.set('items', response)`) so the binding owns rendering, rather than keeping a parallel list in the DOM. Use `CLASS` for screen CSS, `?` for local paths and `data-exec="?/method"` for handlers. Preserve the shell's global model paths.

Treat user text as text in templates; do not add raw HTML rendering or string-built event attributes. Backend view directives (`@{...}`), translation markers (`@(...)`) and client Tangular (`{{ ... }}`) are distinct stages. Use the syntax supported by that app's library and compiler; check a working template for block terminators and escaping.

## Translations and icons

English text is the source key: `@(Save)`, `@(Target URL)`, translated through the app's `.resource` files. Keep resource keys, locale component configuration and any new error text synchronized. Avoid hard-coded translated copies in JS conditionals. Use the existing Total Icons `ti ti-*` assets and names from the app, with a label or accessible name for icon-only controls.

## Reusable components

Look for an existing component first. If new behaviour is reusable, use `COMPONENT('name', function(self, config, cls) { ... })` and the lifecycle supported by the installed jComponent version: build the DOM once, update from its bound value, react to configuration changes and release subscriptions/timers when destroyed. Read an existing component of that version for the exact methods. Keep feature permissions, API URLs and page model names in the plugin rather than baking them into the component.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/cms-widgets.md

# CMS widgets

A CMS widget is a reusable editable content block. Preserve the catalogue's native single-file format, `widgets/<id>.html`; a widget is not a jComponent registration or a standalone web page. Inspect the consuming CMS before choosing APIs: the reference CMS uses Framework 5 on the server and jComponent v19 in the admin. The backend major does not determine the browser UI major.

## Sections

| Section | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `<script total>` | Metadata and optional server hooks |
| `<settings>` | Editor controls and optional settings script/style |
| `<style>` | Widget CSS |
| `<body>` | Initial editable content |
| `<script>` outside settings/body | Optional public browser code |
| `<template>` | Optional render template |
| `<readme>` | Purpose, defaults, allowed values and dependencies |

Use exact lowercase section tags. The CMS extracts settings before other sections, so its nested script/style stay inside settings. Metadata follows existing widgets: `exports.id`, `name`, `author`, `version`, `preview`, and `config` when needed. Match the id and filename; check existing ids and names. Preview is an embedded image, not a separate required catalogue file.

## Scope and settings

The compiler replaces `CLASS` with `w-<normalized-widget-id>` in CSS, settings, body, public JS and template. That prefix belongs to the widget type and is shared by its instances. Scope CSS with `.CLASS`/`.CLASS-...`; change an individual instance through the `el` argument rather than a global selector or fixed DOM id.

Settings controls use `?.key` paths corresponding to defaults in `exports.config`. Their `<script>` may export `check(config, el)`, `load(config, el)` and `save(config, el)`. Defaults must match the initial body. Document finite values such as status/alignment explicitly; validate them before constructing classes or styles. Apply cosmetic changes without replacing edited text, repeated blocks or nested widgets. Repeated saves must be safe.

Use the existing editor markers where appropriate: `CMS_edit`, `CMS_remove`, `CMS_repeat`, `CMS_attribute` and `CMS_widgets` for nested content. Visitor content remains editable content, rather than being converted into fixed admin translation keys. Follow the consuming CMS's localization path for settings UI.

## Server rendering

A static widget normally needs no render hook. A dynamic widget may export `render(opt, next)` in `<script total>`. The CMS supplies instance configuration in `opt.config`, inner markup in `opt.html`, the whole body in `opt.body` and the render template in `opt.template`. Other page/user context is optional.

Call `next(content, replace, cache)` exactly once on success, empty and failure paths. The default keeps the wrapper; `replace: true` removes it. Cache only output that is safe to share within the CMS cache scope. Do not assume incoming saved config contains newly added defaults.

The server script is evaluated before scoping and is not rewritten: never return unresolved CLASS placeholders from a server render hook. Reuse scoped markup or emit known classes explicitly. Encode text inserted into server HTML with `.encode()`; use `.text()` in editor DOM. Public scripts cannot assume the admin's library or state is loaded on every site layout.

## Verification and AI guidance

Give agents the native format, actual hook contracts, compatible examples, a short creation/review workflow and commands that check the artifact. Keep a shared skill/checklist instead of divergent copies for each agent. Generate model indexes from the maintained pages and check links and commands. Preserve existing catalogue files when adding an authoring kit; tooling and examples do not need a catalogue migration.

Check with the real parser/compiler, then browser settings and published rendering. Test edited content, nested slots, repeated saves, two configurations, empty/long/HTML-like text and desktop/mobile widths. Open a screenshot of the final widget before accepting its appearance. Chromium can be installed by Playwright; Chrome is an alternative. An isolated browser harness does not prove complete CMS editor integration. See [native tests](../general/testing.md).

## References

- [CMS definitions/func.js](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/definitions/func.js): FUNC.recompile, sections and CLASS substitution.
- [CMS widget template](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/public/widget.txt), [editor](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/public/cmseditor/index.html), [admin layout](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/views/admin.html): hooks, markers and UI version.
- [Framework 5 cms.js](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/7d2d553fc774090081b4e3b1ae75a52ef06b42b8/cms.js): rendering, wrappers and cache.
- [CMS widget authoring kit](https://github.com/totaljs-es/cms-widgets/blob/63892ff/AGENTS.md): runnable examples, checks, skills and embedded previews.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/css.md

# CSS

- File names lowercase, words separated by `-`.
- **One rule per line**: keep all declarations of a selector on the same line.
- Strings in `'` apostrophes.
- No vendor prefixes: current browsers do not need them. `/*auto*/` at the top of a file comes from Total.js 4, which added them; Total.js 5 keeps the mark and adds nothing.
- No LESS and no SASS: Total.js CSS supports variables and nested selectors.

```css
/*auto*/

.class { key1: value; key2: value; key3: value; }
.class > div { key1: value; key2: value; }
```

## In plugins

Style that belongs to a screen goes at the top of its HTML file, scoped with `CLASS`:

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
	.CLASS .listing2 .permanent { background-color: #F6E7EA; }
</style>
```

`CLASS` becomes a class unique to the plugin, so the rule cannot leak to other screens.

## Predefined classes

The `intranetcss` component provides the common design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode). Use its classes before writing new CSS: see [components](components.md).

## Global style

`public/default.css` holds what is shared. Colors that change per user or theme are CSS variables (`:root { --color: ... }`), set once in the layout.

## Static files

`/img/`, `/css/`, `/js/`, `/fonts/`, `/videos/`. Images use the file-name rule: lowercase with dashes.

## Component skins

Scope overrides to an app class combined with the official component class, for example `.app-backtotop.ui-backtotop`. Keep the official component's selectors and behavior intact. Component CSS can be injected after the app stylesheet; use deliberate specificity instead of depending only on load order or broad global overrides.

Skinning the official BackToTop works this way. Preserve visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, mobile positioning and `prefers-reduced-motion` when adapting its appearance. Semantic or focus changes belong in a small native initialization hook, as described in [components](components.md), rather than in CSS.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/reference/jcomponent/readme.md

# jComponent 20: the official guides

How to use the elements of the interface library of Total.js in HTML, and how to write a component. These pages are the guides of the Total.js team, copied without changes from the repository of the components, so that they are here with the rest:

- Source: <https://github.com/totaljs/components> (`docs/api.md` and `docs/aicontext/`), revision `f3ac05f7`.
- License: MIT, Copyright (c) Peter Širka. The notice is in [LICENSE](LICENSE).
- Update them from the source; do not edit them here.
- `component-development.md` mentions `jcomponent-components.md`, a page that the source does not have either.

| Page | What it is |
|---|---|
| [ui-component.md](aicontext/ui-component.md) | Use a component in HTML with `<ui-component>`: `name`, `path`, `config`, `default` |
| [ui-bind.md](aicontext/ui-bind.md) | Bind data to HTML with `<ui-bind>`: text, HTML, templates, classes, visibility |
| [ui-plugin.md](aicontext/ui-plugin.md) | A screen with its own scope: `<ui-plugin>` and `PLUGIN()` |
| [ui-import.md](aicontext/ui-import.md) | Load a part of the interface when it is needed with `<ui-import>` |
| [api.md](api.md) | The methods of the library and what a component can implement |
| [component-development.md](aicontext/component-development.md) | Write a new component from a description: contract, hooks, data flow, verification |

The catalogue of the published components, with a live preview of each, is <https://componentator.com>. The templates of a `ui-bind` are [Tangular](../../conventions/frontend/tangular.md), and the applications [`apps/board`](../../apps/board) and [`apps/chat`](../../apps/chat) use these elements in screens that were checked in a browser.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/reference/jcomponent/aicontext/ui-component.md

# AI Guide: Initialize jComponent via `<ui-component>`

## Purpose

This document defines how AI should generate a valid base initialization for a selected jComponent after a user prompt, for example:

- `add datagrid component`

The result must be valid HTML (and optional JS) using Total.js UI component rules.

## Source of truth

Use these sources in this order:

1. Official `ui-component` documentation (syntax and binding behavior).
2. Local component index (name, aliases, config keys, example snippet).
3. Component `readme` and `example` data for component-specific details.

## Canonical HTML declaration

```html
<ui-component name="componentname" path="path.to.model" config="key1:value1;key2:value2" default="default_value"></ui-component>
```

Rules:

- `name` is required.
- `path` is optional.
- `config` is optional.
- `default` is optional and evaluated as a raw value/object.

## AI generation policy

### 1) Component resolution

- Resolve component from user prompt via `name` + `aliases`.
- Example: `datagrid` -> `name="datagrid"`.
- If multiple candidates match, pick highest confidence and report alternatives in `warnings`.

### 2) Base initialization output (default mode)

When user asks only to add a component, generate minimum valid initialization:

```html
<ui-component name="{{component_name}}" path="?.example"></ui-component>
```

Default path policy:

- Use `path="?.example"` unless user requests a specific model path.
- Keep output minimal: do not inject non-required config keys.

### 3) Config generation

If user asks for configured initialization, generate `config` using allowed keys from component index/readme only.

Config formatting rules:

- Format: `key1:value1;key2:value2`
- Numbers are plain numeric values, for example `limit:20`
- Booleans are `true`/`false`
- If value contains `:`, escape it as `\:`
- Absolute URLs can remain unescaped (`https://...`)

### 4) Optional `default`

Use `default` only when user asks for initial value.

Example:

```html
<ui-component name="textbox" path="?.name" default="John"></ui-component>
```

### 5) Optional demo structure

If user asks for a demo/working sample, include component-specific starter snippet from index `example` data.

For DataGrid this usually means:

- `<ui-component name="datagrid" ...>`
- inline `<script type="text/plain">[...]</script>` for columns
- small JS block with sample data/callback

## Prompt -> output examples

### Example A: base initialization

Prompt:

- `add datagrid component`

Output:

```html
<ui-component name="datagrid" path="?.example"></ui-component>
```

### Example B: with basic config

Prompt:

- `add datagrid with checkbox and row click handler`

Output:

```html
<ui-component name="datagrid" path="?.example" config="checkbox:true;click:onRowClick"></ui-component>

<script>
	function onRowClick(row, grid, row_el) {
		console.log(row);
	}
</script>
```

## Validation checklist (must pass)

1. Uses `<ui-component ...></ui-component>` tag.
2. Always contains `name`.
3. `name` maps to an existing component in index.
4. Any `config` keys are valid for the selected component.
5. Output HTML is syntactically valid.
6. If JS callbacks are referenced, output includes callback stubs.

## Extended rules from official docs

- Data-binding path is watched by the component.
- Relative pathing in nested plugins/components may use `?` and `@path` patterns.
- Versioned components are allowed (`textbox@1`, `textbox@2`).
- Special config keys are supported (for example `$id`, `$class`, `$binding`, `$delay`, `$init`, `$setter`, `$state`, `$reconfigure`, `$compile`, `$url`).

## Recommended response contract for AI engine

```json
{
  "component": "datagrid",
  "html": "<ui-component name=\"datagrid\" path=\"?.example\"></ui-component>",
  "js": "",
  "warnings": [],
  "notes": []
}
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/reference/jcomponent/aicontext/ui-bind.md

# AI Guide: Use `<ui-bind>` for Data Binding

## Purpose

This document defines how AI should generate valid `<ui-bind>` markup from a user prompt.

Example prompts:

- `add ui-bind for user.name`
- `show text from ?.total`
- `render order items with template`

The output must follow official Total.js UI binding rules.

## Source of truth

Use these sources in this order:

1. Official `<ui-bind>` documentation.
2. Existing project context (requested model path, existing DOM element, callback names).
3. Existing local binding style conventions.

## Canonical declaration

```html
<ui-bind path="path.to.property" config="COMMAND_A;COMMAND_B;COMMAND_N"></ui-bind>
```

Core rules:

- `path` is required in normal mode.
- `config` contains one or multiple bind commands separated by `;`.
- `<ui-bind>` is inline by default (use `class="block"` or `style="display:block"` for block layout).

## Attributes

### `path="..."`

- Path to the model value to watch.
- Updates run when value changes via binding-aware methods.

### `config="..."`

- One or more commands.
- Command format is usually `command:expression`.

### `element="selector"` (optional)

- Applies binding to a selected element instead of the `<ui-bind>` element.
- Do not combine with multi-element selections.

### `parent="selector"` (optional)

- Resolves target in parent nodes instead of the `<ui-bind>` node.

### `child="selector"` (optional)

- Resolves target in child nodes instead of the `<ui-bind>` node.

## AI generation policy

### 1) Default output (minimum valid bind)

When prompt asks to add a bind without extra requirements:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.example" config="text:value"></ui-bind>
```

Default policy:

- Use `path="?.example"` when user does not specify path.
- Prefer `text:value` as safest default command.

### 2) Command selection rules

Select command by user intent:

- plain text rendering -> `text:value`
- HTML rendering -> `html:value`
- show/hide based on condition -> `show:...` or `hide:...`
- call function on change -> `exec:myFunction`
- template rendering list/object -> `template`

### 3) Expression forms

Allowed expression styles:

- direct value: `text:value`
- expression: `text:value.toUpperCase()`
- function link: `exec:myFunction` (must exist in JS scope)
- arrow expression when needed: `hide:n=>!n`

### 4) Template mode

If prompt asks for templating/list rendering, output:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.items" config="template">
	<script type="text/html">
		{{ foreach m in value }}
			<div>{{ m.name }}</div>
		{{ end }}
	</script>
</ui-bind>
```

Template rules:

- use `<script type="text/html">` inside `<ui-bind>`
- in template mode, `value` is the template model from `path`

### 5) Plugin-relative path handling

When prompt is in plugin/nested context, keep relative path conventions (`?.path`, `@path`) according to surrounding code.

### 6) Callback stubs

If `exec:*` is generated and callback does not already exist in local context, generate a JS stub.

## Command quick reference for AI

- `text:value` -> escaped text output
- `html:value` -> raw HTML output
- `show:condition` -> toggles visibility (`hidden` class)
- `hide:condition` -> toggles visibility (`hidden` class)
- `class:classA classB` -> toggles classes
- `exec:handlerName` -> executes handler on value change
- `template` -> Tangular template rendering

## Prompt -> output examples

### Example A: simple text bind

Prompt:

- `bind user name to text`

Output:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.user.name" config="text:value"></ui-bind>
```

### Example B: conditional visibility

Prompt:

- `hide section when cards exist`

Output:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.cards" config="hide:value && value.length > 0">
	<div class="message">No cards</div>
</ui-bind>
```

### Example C: function callback

Prompt:

- `run logic when order status changes`

Output:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.order.status" config="exec:onOrderStatusChanged"></ui-bind>

<script>
	function onOrderStatusChanged(value, path, element) {
		console.log(value);
	}
</script>
```

## Validation checklist (must pass)

1. Uses `<ui-bind ...></ui-bind>` tag.
2. Contains valid `path` unless prompt explicitly requests `path="null"` init style.
3. Uses supported command names in `config`.
4. Expressions are syntactically valid.
5. If `exec:*` is used, callback exists or stub is generated.
6. `template` mode includes `<script type="text/html">` or references a valid external template setup.

## Recommended response contract for AI engine

```json
{
  "binding": "ui-bind",
  "html": "<ui-bind path=\"?.example\" config=\"text:value\"></ui-bind>",
  "js": "",
  "warnings": [],
  "notes": []
}
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/reference/jcomponent/aicontext/ui-plugin.md

# AI Guide: Use `<ui-plugin>` for Scoped UI Composition

## Purpose

This document defines how AI should generate valid `<ui-plugin>` markup from a user prompt.

Example prompts:

- `add ui-plugin for users.form`
- `create anonymous plugin with textbox`
- `wrap these components into isolated plugin`

The output must follow official Total.js plugin/path scoping behavior.

## Source of truth

Use these sources in this order:

1. Official `<ui-plugin>` documentation (including Methods and Properties).
2. Existing project structure and paths.
3. Existing local naming conventions for plugin methods and handlers.

## Canonical declaration

```html
<ui-plugin path="PATH" config="CONFIG">
	<!-- at least one nested <ui-component> or <ui-bind> -->
</ui-plugin>
```

Core rules:

- `path` is required.
- `config` is optional.
- Plugin must contain nested `<ui-component>` or `<ui-bind>`; otherwise plugin is not initialized.

## Why `<ui-plugin>` exists

`<ui-plugin>` reduces repeated full paths in nested UI code.

Without plugin:

```html
<ui-component name="input" path="users.form.firstname"></ui-component>
<ui-component name="input" path="users.form.age"></ui-component>
```

With plugin:

```html
<ui-plugin path="users.form">
	<ui-component name="input" path="?.firstname"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="input" path="?.age"></ui-component>
</ui-plugin>
```

## Plugin methods/properties (v19+ guidance)

When AI generates plugin JS logic, prefer plugin-scoped methods/properties over global state helpers.

Preferred methods:

- `exports.set(path, value)` (or `exports.set(object)`)
- `exports.get(path)`
- `exports.upd(path)`
- `exports.inc(path, value)`
- `exports.push(path, value)`
- `exports.nul(path)`
- `exports.reset([path])`
- `exports.watch(path, callback, [init])`

Useful properties:

- `exports.model` (plugin model)
- `exports.form` (plugin model + state reset behavior)
- `exports.data` (alias to model)
- `exports.name`
- `exports.parent`
- `exports.caller`
- `exports.modified`

Rule for AI:

- If operation targets plugin scope data, use `exports.*` methods first.
- Avoid global `SET('...')` / `GET('...')` for plugin-local state when `exports.*` can do the same.

## AI generation policy

### 1) Default output (minimum valid plugin)

When prompt asks only to add a plugin, generate:

```html
<ui-plugin path="?.example">
	<ui-bind path="?.ready" config="text:value"></ui-bind>
</ui-plugin>
```

Default path policy:

- If user provides explicit path, use it.
- If not provided, use `path="?.example"`.
- Always include at least one nested binder/component.

### 2) Nested component path policy

Inside plugin, prefer relative scoped paths:

- `?.field`
- `?.section.value`

Do not duplicate absolute prefix if plugin path already provides scope.

### 3) Config generation

Supported plugin config keys:

- `init:path.to.method` -> runs on plugin init (`function(plugin, el)`)
- `class:class_name` -> toggles class on plugin element
- `isolated:true` -> plugin does not inherit parent plugin scope
- `aclass:true` -> adds plugin path as class name
- `delay:number` -> class toggle delay (default `300`)

Generate only keys requested by user (or required by context).

### 4) Anonymous plugin generation

If prompt requests anonymous/reusable part, generate `path="?"` or named anonymous variant:

```html
<ui-plugin path="? contactform" config="init:?/init">
	<ui-component name="textbox" path="?.name">Name</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>
```

If code includes JS plugin declaration, use matching name:

```javascript
PLUGIN('contactform', function(exports) {
	exports.init = function() {};
});
```

### 5) Isolated mode in nested plugins

If prompt says "do not inherit parent scope", generate `isolated:true`:

```html
<ui-plugin path="products.form" config="isolated:true">
	<ui-component name="textbox" path="?.name">Name</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>
```

### 6) Parent-scope skipping

If prompt requests skipping parent scope levels, use `?N` form in nested paths:

- `?.name` -> full inherited path
- `?1.name` -> skip one plugin level
- `?2.name` -> skip two plugin levels

## Prompt -> output examples

### Example A: simple scoped container

Prompt:

- `add ui-plugin with path users.form and two inputs`

Output:

```html
<ui-plugin path="users.form">
	<ui-component name="input" path="?.firstname">First name</ui-component>
	<ui-component name="input" path="?.age">Age</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>
```

### Example B: isolated nested plugin

Prompt:

- `inside users.form add isolated plugin products.form with textbox name`

Output:

```html
<ui-plugin path="users.form">
	<ui-plugin path="products.form" config="isolated:true">
		<ui-component name="textbox" path="?.name">Name</ui-component>
	</ui-plugin>
</ui-plugin>
```

### Example C: anonymous plugin

Prompt:

- `create anonymous plugin contactform with init handler and name textbox`

Output:

```html
<ui-plugin path="? contactform" config="init:?/init">
	<ui-component name="textbox" path="?.name">Name</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>

<script>
	PLUGIN('contactform', function(exports) {
		exports.init = function() {
			// plugin initialized
		};
	});
</script>
```

## Validation checklist (must pass)

1. Uses `<ui-plugin ...></ui-plugin>` tag.
2. Contains `path`.
3. Contains at least one nested `<ui-component>` or `<ui-bind>`.
4. Nested paths use plugin scope correctly (`?.*`, `?N.*`, or explicit absolute path where required).
5. Uses only supported plugin config keys.
6. If `init:*` is referenced, function exists or stub is generated.
7. Anonymous plugin naming is consistent between HTML and `PLUGIN(...)` declaration.
8. Plugin-local model changes in JS use `exports.*` methods (not global `SET/GET`) when applicable.

## Recommended response contract for AI engine

```json
{
  "container": "ui-plugin",
  "html": "<ui-plugin path=\"users.form\"><ui-component name=\"input\" path=\"?.firstname\"></ui-component></ui-plugin>",
  "js": "",
  "warnings": [],
  "notes": []
}
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/reference/jcomponent/aicontext/ui-import.md

# AI Guide: Use `<ui-import>` for Dynamic Content Import

## Purpose

This document defines how AI should generate valid `<ui-import>` markup from a user prompt.

Typical prompts:

- `add ui-import for /forms/user.html`
- `import form into #container and replace it`
- `import content with path and id placeholders`

## Source of truth

Use these sources in this order:

1. Official `<ui-import>` documentation and command list.
2. Existing project structure (target element, path conventions, function names).
3. Existing local style conventions.

## Canonical usage

```html
<ui-import config="url:/mysubpage.html"></ui-import>
```

`<ui-import>` dynamically imports content/components into the DOM.

## AI generation policy

### 1) Minimum valid output

When user asks only to add import:

```html
<ui-import config="url:/forms/example.html"></ui-import>
```

### 2) Config formatting

- Config is a semicolon-separated string: `key1:value1;key2:value2`.
- Include only keys requested by the user.
- Keep `url` always present.

### 3) Targeted import vs inline import

- Use `<ui-import ...>` when import belongs to current markup position.
- Use `target:selector` when user explicitly asks to inject content into another element.

### 4) Replace vs append behavior

- Use `replace:true` when user asks to replace current element.
- If `replace:true` is missing, content is appended (default behavior).

### 5) Placeholder replacement support

If imported content contains placeholders:

- `~ID~` -> provide `id:value`
- `~PATH~` -> provide `path:value`

### 6) Hooks and transformation

- `init:path.to.method` runs after import.
- `make:path.to.method` (v18/v19) runs before import and must return updated response string.

### 7) Script/style re-evaluation

- Default behavior evaluates scripts/styles one time.
- Use `reevaluate:true` only when user explicitly needs repeated re-evaluation.

## Commands reference

### `url:value`

Required in practice. URL can be relative or absolute; content is downloaded and imported automatically.

### `init:path.to.method`

Optional. Executes method after content import.

### `target:selector`

Optional. Imports content into a specific target (jQuery selector).

### `replace:true` (v18/v19)

Optional. Replaces current element with imported content. Default is append (`false`).

### `reevaluate:true` (v18/v19)

Optional. Re-evaluates scripts/styles again. Default: `false`.

### `id:value`

Optional. Replaces all `~ID~` placeholders in imported response before evaluation.

Example:

```html
<div data-import="url:/someform.html;id:user.profile"></div>
```

Then `~ID~.name` becomes `user.profile.name`.

### `path:value` (v18/v19)

Optional. Replaces all `~PATH~` placeholders in imported response before evaluation.

Example:

```html
<div data-import="url:/someform.html;path:user.profile"></div>
```

Then `~PATH~.name` becomes `user.profile.name`.

### `class:value`

Optional. Toggles class/classes on the current element after import.

### `cache:value` (v18/v19)

Optional. Enables `localStorage` caching for future usage.

Examples:

- `cache:1 day`
- `cache:10 minutes`

### `make:path.to.method` (v18/v19)

Optional. Executes method before import. Method receives response and must return updated response.

If method returns empty/null, content is not imported.

Example signature:

```js
function updateSomething(response, el, path) {
	return response + '<div>MY ADDITIONAL CONTENT</div>';
}
```

## Static inline variables (`+v19`)

Supported in imported content (`ui-import` and `IMPORT()`):

```html
--VARIABLENAME1=variablevalue1--
--VARIABLENAME2=variablevalue2--

<div>--VARIABLENAME1--</div>
<div>--VARIABLENAME2--</div>
```

## Prompt -> output examples

### Example A: basic import

Prompt:

- `add ui-import for /forms/user.html`

Output:

```html
<ui-import config="url:/forms/user.html"></ui-import>
```

### Example B: replace and target

Prompt:

- `import /forms/user.html into #content and replace`

Output:

```html
<ui-import config="url:/forms/user.html;target:#content;replace:true"></ui-import>
```

### Example C: placeholders with post-init

Prompt:

- `import profile form with id user.profile and run init`

Output:

```html
<ui-import config="url:/forms/profile.html;id:user.profile;init:profile_init"></ui-import>
```

## Validation checklist (must pass)

1. Uses `<ui-import ...></ui-import>` or valid equivalent import declaration.
2. `config` contains `url`.
3. All used command keys are supported commands.
4. `target` uses valid selector when present.
5. `init`/`make` function links point to existing or generated stubs.
6. `replace`, `reevaluate` use boolean values (`true/false`).
7. `id`/`path` are present when placeholders `~ID~`/`~PATH~` are expected.

## Recommended response contract for AI engine

```json
{
  "element": "ui-import",
  "html": "<ui-import config=\"url:/forms/example.html\"></ui-import>",
  "js": "",
  "warnings": [],
  "notes": []
}
```

---

# jComponent API reference

Short reference for writing components for the Total.js UI library (jComponent `v20`, `https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js`). The part below "Generated list" is extracted from the doc comments of the library source; the rest comes from how the existing components use it.

## The component function

```js
COMPONENT(name, config, function(self, config, cls, element) { ... });
```

- `name` is lower case, without `j-`. It is used in HTML as `<ui-component name="name" path="path" config="key:value;key2:value">`.
- `config` is a configuration string `key:value;key2:value` with the defaults. Values are parsed: `10` is a number, `true`/`false` booleans. The tag's `config` attribute overrides them.
- `self` is the instance, `config` the parsed configuration object, `cls` the CSS class `ui-<name>`, `element` the jQuery element.
- `self.element` is the jQuery element, `self.dom` the DOM element, `self.path` the bound path, `self.id` the instance id.

## Members you implement (all optional)

Implement only what the behaviour needs; an empty stub is not an implementation.

| Member | When it runs |
| --- | --- |
| `self.init = function()` | once for the component type, before the first instance's `make` (shared resources, `Thelpers`; never per-instance data) |
| `self.make = function()` | once per instance (build the DOM, register delegated events) |
| `self.setter = function(value, path, flags)` | the model changed, including the first time. `flags` is an object in v20 (not the old numeric `type`) |
| `self.setter2 = function(value, path, flags)` | observes rendering without replacing an inherited setter |
| `self.getter = function(value, realtime)` | parses a user input; keep the built-in unless parsing really needs it, because overriding replaces its model-writing pipeline |
| `self.validate = function(value)` | returns `true` when valid (used with `config.required`) |
| `self.configure = function(key, value, init, previous)` | a configuration key changed; called per key after `make` and on `self.reconfigure(...)`; `init` is `true` on the first pass |
| `self.state = function(type, what)` | the state changed (touched, modified, invalid...) |
| `self.resize = function()` | the window or the parent was resized (debounce it with `setTimeout2`) |
| `self.destroy = function()` | the instance was removed: clean timers, observers, outside-DOM events, subscriptions, requests, third-party widgets. Only when something is owned |

State is public in `config.disabled`, `config.touched`, `config.modified` and `config.invalid`, with the matching state classes. A disabled component must reject interactions, not only look disabled.

## Instance reference (`self`)

Properties: `self.name`, `self.id`, `self.path`, `self.ID`, `self.element` (jQuery), `self.dom` (DOM element), `self.config`.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `self.aclass(cls, [timeout])` | add a class (optionally for a time) |
| `self.rclass(cls, [timeout])` | remove a class (optionally after a time); without arguments removes all |
| `self.rclass2(search)` | remove the classes that contain `search` (`rclass2('ti-')`) |
| `self.tclass(cls, [bool])` / `self.hclass(cls)` | toggle / has class |
| `self.attr(name, [value])` | read or write an attribute |
| `self.css(name, value)` or `self.css(obj)` | styles |
| `self.html(value)` / `self.empty()` / `self.append(html)` | content |
| `self.find(selector)` | find inside the element |
| `self.event(name, [selector], fn)` | event; delegate with a selector, bind once in `make` |
| `self.get()` | read the model value |
| `self.set(value, [flags])` | programmatic write; calls `setter` |
| `self.rewrite(value, [flags])` | write without calling `setter` |
| `self.modify(value, [flags])` | **user interaction**: writes, marks touched/modified and calls `setter` |
| `self.push(value)` | push to an array model |
| `self.update([flags])` / `self.refresh()` | notify the model watchers / call `setter` again |
| `self.change([bool])` | mark the component as changed (dirty) |
| `self.watch(path, fn, [autoinit])` / `self.unwatch(path, [fn])` | watch another path; callback is `(value, flags, path)` |
| `self.datasource(path, fn, [init])` | like `watch`, the new source replaces the previous one |
| `self.reconfigure(config)` | change the configuration (string or object); calls `configure` |
| `self.validate2()` / `self.isInvalid()` | run the validation / read the result |
| `self.singleton()` | one instance for the whole page |
| `self.autobind20(delay, realtimebinding)` | automatic binding of native text/select controls |
| `self.EXEC(path, ...args)` | execute a linked function (`config.change`); keeps the `?/handler` resolution |
| `self.makepath(path)` | resolve `?` to the path of the parent plugin |

**Avoid** (verified in `library.js` 20.014): `self.nocompile()`, `self.release()` and `self.bindvisible()` are no-ops; `self.readonly()` clears `getter` and `setter` at the moment it is called (it is not the HTML `readonly` property): call it before you define them, as the existing components do, never after; do not invent `self.compile()`, `self.novalidate()` or `self.notify()`; do not call `$`-prefixed members (`$setter`, `$validate`...).

Direction of the data: `model change -> setter -> DOM` and `user interaction -> normalize -> self.modify -> setter -> DOM`. The setter renders only: it must not write the value back or fire the user-change callback.

## Paths

- `path="form.name"` binds to `GET('form.name')` and `SET('form.name', value)`.
- `?` is replaced by the path of the parent `<ui-plugin>` (`self.makepath('?.items')`). A leading `*` is the common path prefix of the library (the example uses `path="*form"`).
- `SET`, `GET`, `UPD`, `PUSH`, `CMD`, `EXEC` and `SETTER('component/method', ...args)` work from outside the component. `SETTER('example/reconfigure', 'title:New')` calls the method on every instance of the component `example`; `SETTER(true, 'example/method', ...)` waits until the component is ready.

## Dark and large mode

The library toggles classes on `body`: `ui-dark` and `ui-large`. To try them in an example:

```js
APPEARANCE({ dark: true });
APPEARANCE({ dark: false, large: true });
```

The CSS variables `--color`, `--rgb`, `--radius`, `--gap` and `--margin` can be changed in the same call (`APPEARANCE({ color: '#E91E63' })`).

## Icons

Total.js icons: `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. `self.icon(value)` adds the prefix when the config value has none.

## Generated list

## Component

- `instance.readonly()`: The library comment says "disables validation", but in v20 it also clears `getter` and `setter` when it is called: call it before defining them.
- `instance.singleton()`: The method enables changes the component instance to a singleton.
- `instance.set(value, [flags])` (value {String}; [flags] {String} with @): The method assigns a value to the model and calls `setter`.
- `instance.rewrite(value, [flags])` (value {String}; [flags] {String} with @): The method assigns a value to the model without calling the setter.
- `instance.get()`: The method reads a value from the model.
- `instance.on(name, callback)`: The method registers a global event.
- `instance.watch(path, callback)`: The method registers a new watcher to capture changes based on the path.
- `instance.unwatch(path, [callback])`: The method unregisters an existing watcher.
- `instance.emit(name, [a], [b], [c], [d])`: The method emits a global event within Total.js UI library.
- `instance.parent(selector)` (selector {String}): The method tries to find parent element according to the selector.
- `instance.modify(value, [type])`: The method assigns a value to the model, sets a state to `touched` and calls `setter`.
- `instance.touch()`: The method simulates user "touch".
- `instance.reset()`: The method resets the state.
- `instance.reconfigure(value)`: The method reconfigures the component. The `value` can be `String` or `Object`.
- `instance.refresh()`: The method refreshes value (in other words, it calls instance.setter()).
- `instance.command(name, callback)` (name {String}; callback {Function(a, b, c, d, e)}): The method registers a new command.
- `instance.CMD(name, [a], [b], [c], [d])` (name {String}; [a] {Object}; [b] {Object}; [c] {Object}; [d] {Object}): The method executes a command with custom arguments.
- `instance.icon(value)` (value {String}): The method checks if it is needed to add the icon prefix defined in `DEF.iconprefix`.
- `instance.caniuse(name)` (name {String}; return {String}): The method checks if the component `name` is defined or not. You can use multiple names in the form `message|notify`.
- `instance.replace(target, [remove])` (target {Element/jQuery}; [remove] {Boolean}): The method moves the component into another element defined in the `target` argument.

## Globals

- `NOOP()` (return {Function}): The method returns empty function that means "no operation".
- `inDOM(element)` (element {Element}; return {Boolean}): The method returns if the element is attached in the DOM.
- `ON(name, callback)` (name {String}; callback {Function(a, b, c, d)}): The method registers a new handler for capturing a specific event.
- `OFF(name, [callback])` (name {String}; [callback] {Function}): The method removes the existing handler for capturing a specific event.
- `EMIT(name, [a], [b], [c], [d])` (name {String}; [a] {Object}; [b] {Object}; [c] {Object}; [d] {Object}): The method emits a specific event to all plugins and components.
- `ATTRD(el, attrd)` (el {jQuery/Element}; attrd {String} attribute name (default: `id`); return {String}): The method tries to read closest `data-{attrd}` value.
- `SET(path, value)` (path {String}; value {Object}): The method sets and notifies all UI components and watchers based on the path.
- `GET(path)` (path {String}; return {Object}): Based on the path, the method returns a value.
- `UPD(path)` (path {String}): The method notifies all UI components and watchers based on the path.
- `COMPONENTS(path)` (path {String}): The method returns all components on the specific path. It supports flags @touched, @visible, @modified, @invalid, @disabled, @enabled, @required
- `COMPONENT(name, [config], callback, [dependencies])` (path {String}; [config] {Object}; callback {Function(self, config, cls, element)}; [dependencies] {String}): The method registers a new component declaration.
- `PLUGIN(path, [config], callback, [dependencies])` (path {String}; [config] {Object}; callback {Function(self, config, element, cls)}; [dependencies] {String}): The method registers a new plugin declaration.
- `ERRORS(path, callback)` (path {String|jQuery Element}; callback {Function(arr)}): The method returns errors based on the path in the callback argument.
- `HIDDEN(el)` (el {jQuery/Element}): The method determines whether the element is visible or not.
- `VISIBLE(el, [threshold], [mode])` (el {jQuery/Element}; [threshold] {Number}; mode {visible|above|below}; return {Boolean}): The method checks if the element is visible on the screen.
- `NOTFOCUSED()` (return {Boolean}): The method checks if the browser window is focused or not.
- `SCROLLBAR(element, options)` (element {String/jQuery/Element}; options {Object}; return {Scrollbar}): The method wraps the `element` with a custom scrollbar.
- `SCROLLBARWIDTH()` (return {Number}): The method returns the width of the scrollbar.
- `WIDTH(element)` (element {String/jQuery}; return {Number}): The method returns the element's width.
- `ENV(name, value)` (name {String}; value {String}): The method registers a new environment variable.
- `ENV(name)` (name {String}; returns {String}): The method reads the value of the environment variable.
- `HASH(value)` (value {String/Number/Boolean/Object/Date}): The method creates a hash from the `value`.
- `WARN(a, [b], [c], [d])` (a {Object}; [b] {Object}; [c] {Object}; [d] {Object}): The method prints a warning on the web dev console.
- `GUID([length])` (length {Number}): The method generates a unique identifier randomly. The `length {Number}` argument can affect its length.
- `AJAX(url, [data], callback)` (url {String}; [data] {Object}; callback {Function(response)}, #onprogress {Function(percentage)}): The method parsers JSON and converts all dates to `Date` object.
- `ADAPT(path, id, text)` (path {String}; id {String}; text {String}; return {String}): The method replaces all keywords `CLASS` and `~PATH~` for the `path` value, and `~ID~` for the `id` value in the `text` argument.
- `IMPORT(url, [target], callback)` (url {String}; [target] {String/jQuery/Element}; callback {Function}): The method imports external sources like JavaScript libaries, CSS libraries, UI components or parts. Supported flags: @prepend, @singleton, <global_variable_name>, url .extension, .
- `PARSE(value)` (value {String}; return {Object}): The method parsers JSON and converts all dates to `Date` object.
- `CACHE(key, value, expire)` (key {String}; value {Object}; expire {String}): @Method: CACHE(key); #key {String}; #return {Object}; The method reads or writes persistent data into the `localStorage`.
- `LOCALIZE(text)` (text {String}; return {String}): The method loads a localization dictionary. The format must be the same as the Total.js resource file.
- `LOCALIZE(text)` (text {String}; return {String}): The method translates the Total.js localization markup as `@(text to translate)`. The localization dictionary must be loaded via the `LOCALIZE()` method.
- `ERROR(response, success, error)` (response {Object}; success {Function(response)}; error {Function(response)}): The method processes errors.
- `EXTENSION(name, config, callback)` (name {String}; config {String/Object}; callback {Function(instance, config, element, cls)}): The method extends UI components `component_name` or plugins `@plugin_name`.
- `CONFIG(selector, config)` (selector {String/Function(instance)}; config {String/Object}): The method reconfigure all existing and new components. Possible selectors: `#component_id`, `.component_path`, `component_name`.

## Path

- `instance.includes(path)` (path {String}; partially {Boolean}; return {Boolean}): The method checks to see if the path is part of the route.
- `instance.assign(path)` (path {String}): The method assigns a new path to the current path instance.
- `instance.get(scope)` (scope {Object}): The method reads a `value` based on a `path` in the defined `scope`.
- `instance.set(scope, value)` (scope {Object}; value {String/Number/Boolean/Object/Date}): The method assigns a `value` based on a `path` to the defined `scope`.
- `instance.notify(scope)` (scope {Object}): The method notifies all watchers based on the path.
- `instance.exec([callback])` ([callback] {Function()}): The method executes flags and code lists.
- `instance.find(scope, callback)` (scope {object}; callback {Function(arr)}): The method returns in the callback all component instances defined in the path scope.

## jQuery extensions

- `$(selector).multiple({ input: 'selector', textarea: 'selector' })`: The method searches for all elements based on the object keys.
- `$(selector).autofocus([selector])`: The method performs auto-focus for `selector`. Default: `selector` value `input,textarea,select`.
- `$(selector).plugin()`: The method finds the closest plugin.
- `$(selector).aclass(cls, [timeout])`: The method appends CSS class to the current element.
- `$(selector).rclass(cls, [timeout])`: The method removes CSS class from the current element.
- `$(selector).rattr(name)`: The method removes attribute.
- `$(selector).rattrd(name)`: The method removes `data` attribute.
- `$(selector).rclass2(find, [timeout])`: The method removes all CSS classes that contain the `find` phrase.
- `$(selector).hclass(name)`: The method checks if the element contains a defined CSS class.
- `$(selector).tclass(name, [enable])`: The method toggles the CSS class for the current element.
- `$(selector).attrd(name, value)`: The method assigns a `value` to the current element's specific attribute `name`.
- `$(selector).attrd2(name, value)`: The method tries to find a data attribute value in the parent tree of the current element.
- `$(selector).asvg(tag)`: The method creates an SVG element.

## String.prototype

- `String.prototype.parseConfig([def], [noconvert])` (def {String|Object} a default configuration; noconvert {Boolean} disables number/boolean/datetime conversation; returns {Object}): The method parses Total.js UI library configuration in the form `key1:value;key2:value`.
- `String.prototype.isJSONDate()` (return {Boolean}): The method checks if the string is a serialized JSON date.
- `String.prototype.VARIABLES(args)` (args {Object}; return {String}): The method applies `--VARIABLE--` defined in the `args` argument in the current string.
- `String.prototype.args(obj, [encode])` (obj {Object} payload, #encode {String/Function(key, value)} supported values `json`, `escape` and `encode`; return {String}): The method checks if the string is a serialized JSON date.

## String prototype

- `String.prototype.format([index0], [index1], [index2])`: The method replaces all indexes in the form `{index}` with values defined as arguments.
- `String.prototype.env()`: The method replaces all phrases `[key]` with values defined in the environment.

## Array.prototype

- `Array.prototype.group(key)` (return {Array}): The method groups items according to the @key field.
- `Array.prototype.trim()` (return {Array}): The method trims all string values, and empty values will be skipped.

## Date.prototype

- `Date.prototype.add(value)` (value {String} #return {Date}): The method extends the current `Date` with the declared `value`.

## Plugin

- `instance.parent(selector)` (selector {String}): The method tries to find parent element according to the selector.
- `instance.get(path)`: The method reads a value from the plugin model.
- `instance.set(path, value)`: The method assigns a `value` based on a `path` to the defined plugin `scope`.
- `instance.push(path, value)`: The method pushes a `value` based on a `path` to the defined plugin `scope`.
- `instance.inc(path, value)`: The method increments a `value` based on a `path` to the defined plugin `scope`.
- `instance.toggle(path)`: The method toggles a `value` based on a `path` to the defined plugin `scope`.
- `instance.set(path, value)`: The method assigns a `value` based on a `path` to the defined plugin `scope`.
- `instance.update(path)`: The method notifies all components and watchers based on the path.
- `instance.on(name, callback)`: The method registers a global event.
- `instance.emit(name, [a], [b], [c], [d])`: The method emits a global event within Total.js UI library.
- `instance.watch(path, callback)`: The method registers a new watcher to capture changes based on the path.

## Core

- `jComponent.free()`: The method clears all removed components, binders and plugins.
- `jComponent.set(scope, path, value)` (scope {Object}; path {String}; value {Object}): The method assigns a `value` based on a `path` to the defined `scope`.
- `jComponent.get(scope, path)` (scope {Object}; path {String}; return {String/Boolean/Object}): The method reads a `value` based on a `path` in the defined `scope`.
- `jComponent.find(scope, path, callback)` (scope {object}; path {String}; callback {Function(arr)}): The method returns in the callback all component instances defined in the path scope.
- `jComponent.notify(scope, path, [onlyflags])` (scope {Object}; path {String}; onlyflags {Boolean} optional default "false"): The method notifies all watchers based on a `path` ot the defined `scope`.
- `jComponent.cl(name, callback)` (name {String}; callback {Function()}): The method inicializes codelists.
