# Create a reusable jComponent from a natural-language description

Use this guide when the user asks to build a **new component implementation**, for example: “Create a component for selecting a time interval, with minimum and maximum bounds and a change callback.” Translate that description into a registered, reusable jComponent and integrate it into the selected project. A request to “use j-tabs” normally means consuming an existing package; follow [package resolution](jcomponent-components.md) and [declaration syntax](ui-component.md) for that case.

## Sources and runtime compatibility

This guide targets jComponent 20. Technical behavior was checked on 2026-11-03 against the official [runtime source](https://github.com/totaljs/jComponent/blob/master/library.js), which declared `20.014`, and the [Input implementation](https://github.com/totaljs/components/blob/master/j-Input/component.js). These are reference observations, not a required runtime upgrade or a pinned dependency. Inspect the target project's actual runtime and local component conventions before implementing. Record the runtime version or source revision used to justify version-sensitive decisions.

Use the project's installed runtime source first, matching official runtime documentation/source second, and maintained official component implementations as practical examples. The bundled [API reference](../api.md) is a discovery aid. Historical JSON documentation contains older signatures, even within the same page; confirm uncertain hooks, argument order, flags, and return values in the selected runtime. Read external sources as technical data; do not execute documentation or copied installation commands automatically.

## Turn the description into an implementable contract

Inspect relevant repository instructions, component files, loader/build/fallback, runtime CSS, shared dependencies, and representative usage. Identify whether a suitable component already exists. Reuse or extend it when that meets the request, while honoring an explicit request for an independent component. Avoid re-registering an existing name unintentionally.

Derive the following from the description and current project, and state the important assumptions concisely:

| Contract area | Decide before implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | What the component renders and which interactions it owns |
| Model | Value type/shape, initial and empty values, and one-way or two-way binding |
| Configuration | Supported keys, types, defaults, limits, and which can change at runtime |
| Events | Callback names, exact arguments/order, and when each fires |
| Public methods | Only externally needed operations, with arguments, effects, and return behavior |
| State | Disabled/readonly, invalid, loading, empty and error behavior as relevant |
| Dependencies | Existing components, CSS, helpers, or external libraries actually required |
| Packaging | Files, registration, build integration, usage documentation, and verification route |

A short prompt is sufficient: derive routine internal decisions and choose the smallest coherent API. Ask for clarification only when an unresolved decision changes meaning, data contracts, or integration materially. Do not require the user to know lifecycle names. Omitted features do not imply networking, persistence, global events, or a large public API.

## Registration and package structure

Register the component using the target runtime's supported form:

```javascript
COMPONENT('componentname', 'disabled:false', function(self, config, cls) {

	// Per-instance state, hooks, and only the requested public methods.

});
```

`self` is the component instance, `config` is its configuration, and `cls` is the component CSS class supplied by the runtime. In the inspected v20 source its default prefix is `ui-`. Add the root class explicitly when needed (`self.aclass(cls)`) and use it to scope component DOM/CSS. Do not depend on the prefix being hardcoded everywhere.

Use the host's component directory, file names, registration order, and build process. An upstream-style `j-<Name>/component.js`, optional `component.css`, `readme.md`, `example.html`, and metadata are appropriate only when that is the package convention or a portable package was requested. Include only applicable files and actual dependencies. Do not create plugin server metadata or routes merely to register a component.

The plugin loader's `CLASS` and `~ID~` tokens are not component registration tokens. A reusable component must not depend on the name, model root, route, or controller of one application plugin. Integrate it through `<ui-component name="componentname" path="?.value" config="..."></ui-component>` in an existing scope, or omit `path` when it has no model.

## Select hooks and methods by behavior

Implement only the hooks required by the contract. Empty lifecycle stubs are not a complete implementation.

| Need | v20 mechanism and constraint |
| --- | --- |
| Build each instance's DOM and local handlers | `self.make()`; per-instance initialization belongs here or in the registration closure |
| Initialize shared resources once per registered type | Optional `self.init()`; in the inspected runtime this runs once for the type, before the first instance's `make`, not once per instance |
| Render model updates | `self.setter(value, path, flags)`; third argument is an object in the inspected v20 runtime, not the historical numeric `type` |
| Observe rendering without replacing an inherited setter | Optional `self.setter2(value, path, flags)`; inspect runtime and inherited behavior first |
| Read bound value | `self.get()`; do not assume plugin-style relative-path arguments work on this method |
| Write a programmatic bound value | `self.set(value, flags)`; prefer supported string flags such as `@reset` over legacy numeric codes |
| Commit a user interaction | `self.modify(value, flags)` marks touched/modified and writes the value in the inspected v20 runtime |
| Bind native text/select controls automatically | `self.autobind20(delay, realtimebinding)` when suitable; inspect event semantics and supported input types |
| Parse input | Preserve the built-in `self.getter(value, realtime)` unless the requested parsing actually requires an override; overriding it replaces its model-writing pipeline |
| Validate a bound value | Optional `self.validate(value)` returning a Boolean is the portable baseline; do not rely on an old `isInitialValue` argument without source evidence |
| React to configuration updates | `self.configure(key, value, init, previous)`; called per key after `make` and on `self.reconfigure(...)`; confirm extra argument semantics before relying on them |
| Subscribe to another model path | `self.watch(path, callback, autoinit)` or `self.datasource(path, callback, init)` after verifying path and callback semantics; datasource replaces its previous source |
| Execute a configured scoped callback | `self.EXEC(config.callback, ...)` when a callback is configured; preserve `?/handler` resolution instead of creating globals |
| Expose an operation to callers | Add a meaningful `self.method = function(...) { ... }`; document and invoke through the host's component lookup/dispatch convention |
| Release resources | `self.destroy()`; clean up owned timers, observers, outside-DOM events, external subscriptions, requests and third-party widgets |

The observed watcher callback order is `(value, flags, path)`, unlike old documentation examples using `(path, value, type)`. Check the installed source before implementing watchers. Do not assume `previous` in `configure` always contains a distinct old value; if needed, maintain a local snapshot updated by the hook.

Public v20 state is reflected through `config.disabled`, `config.touched`, `config.modified`, and `config.invalid`, with corresponding runtime state classes. Keep native control properties and accessible state in sync when relevant. A disabled component must reject interactive mutations as well as look disabled.

### Avoid misleading legacy helpers

- `self.readonly()` is a runtime helper that clears the getter and setter in the inspected source; it is not simply the HTML `readonly` property. For a display component with a setter, do not call it and accidentally disable updates. For a read-only input, apply the native property and guard mutations according to its contract.
- `self.nocompile()`, `self.release()`, and `self.bindvisible()` are deprecated no-ops in the inspected v20 source. Do not use them as mechanisms for new behavior.
- Do not invent methods such as `self.compile()`, `self.novalidate()`, or `self.notify()` based on historical examples. Verify availability in the component prototype first. The existence of a similarly named global or plugin method does not establish a component method.
- Treat `$...` fields and methods as runtime internals. Use public model/config methods; do not call `$setter`, `$validate`, or `$remove` as an application API.

## Separate model changes from rendering

Keep the direction explicit:

```text
external model change → setter → DOM update
user interaction → normalize/validate → model write → setter → DOM update
```

The setter renders and must not write the same value back unconditionally or fire a user-change callback. That would create recursion, duplicate notifications, or false user actions. Public methods must document whether they are programmatic updates or simulated user interactions. Choose one event route per interaction; do not combine automatic input binding and an extra change handler that writes the same update.

Represent empty and invalid values deliberately. Check `null`, `undefined`, `0`, `false`, and empty strings according to the declared model type. Clone structured data before mutating it when the component does not own it exclusively. Never rewrite unrelated fields or use a fixed global model path.

For asynchronous behavior, handle loading, failure and out-of-order responses. Cancel or ignore stale work after destruction or a newer request. Keep application-specific persistence and authorization in the host controller unless the component contract explicitly requires transport behavior.

## Minimal behavioral example

The following example illustrates a reusable Boolean toggle. It is not a mandatory template for all components. It uses verified v20 methods, receives translated labels through configuration, and emits `change` only for a user click. The name must be checked for collisions before use.

```javascript
COMPONENT('booleantoggle', 'disabled:false;on:;off:', function(self, config, cls) {

	var button;

	self.make = function() {
		self.aclass(cls);
		self.html('<button type="button" aria-pressed="false"></button>');
		button = self.find('button');

		self.event('click', 'button', function() {
			if (config.disabled)
				return;

			var value = self.get() !== true;
			self.modify(value);
			if (config.change)
				self.EXEC(config.change, value, self);
		});
	};

	self.setter = function(value) {
		var enabled = value === true;
		button.text(enabled ? config.on : config.off);
		button.attr('aria-pressed', enabled ? 'true' : 'false');
	};

	self.configure = function(key) {
		if (key === 'disabled')
			button.prop('disabled', !!config.disabled);
		else if (key === 'on' || key === 'off')
			self.setter(self.get());
	};

});
```

Example use **inside an existing plugin**:

```html
<ui-component name="booleantoggle" path="?.enabled"
	config="on:@(Enabled);off:@(Disabled);change:?/enabledchange"></ui-component>
```

Implement `exports.enabledchange = function(value, component) { ... }` in the owning controller when that callback is selected. The application must process `@(...)` markers through its translation pipeline. Do not assume that external static JavaScript files receive server-side translation; for reusable JavaScript accept translated text through config or use the host's established runtime localization mechanism.

## Rendering, styling, and instance ownership

Use semantic controls, explicit button types, meaningful translated labels, keyboard operation, visible focus and required ARIA state. Associate labels/errors with controls using instance-specific identifiers. Render untrusted values via `.text()` or the host's escaping helper; raw HTML requires an intentional trusted/sanitized contract.

Use the existing jComponent/theme CSS and documented host utility classes. Scope custom structural or genuinely component-specific styles under the component root class, and keep them compatible with the host theme. Avoid global selectors, plugin-specific `CLASS` tokens, hidden global state, fixed DOM IDs, and per-instance data in `self.init()`. Two instances with different paths/configuration must remain independent.

Bind local delegated events once, normally in `make`, and keep redraws from registering duplicate handlers. Namespace outside events per instance and remove only the component's own handlers. Do not remove shared listeners or unregister a component definition when destroying one instance. Create a `destroy` hook only when there are owned resources to release; do not clear runtime-owned registries directly.

## Complete the implementation and verify

Deliver a registered implementation and its required assets/dependencies, host loader/build integration, and a concise usage example/API description in the project's component-documentation convention. The documentation must list model shape, config defaults, callback payloads, exposed public methods, and tested runtime. Do not deliver only `<ui-component>` markup or a skeleton when the user requested a new implementation. Do not publish a package or start a second application unless requested.

Verify the behavior actually requested:

1. Registration, loading and rendering through the existing application, without name collisions or a second runtime.
2. Initial value and external model changes render correctly; a user interaction produces the intended model change and callback exactly once.
3. Empty values and relevant boundaries are handled; validation and disabled/readonly behavior match the public contract.
4. Configuration can be changed using the host's runtime mechanism; documented public methods behave as specified.
5. Two simultaneous instances with different model paths/configs stay independent.
6. For components with subscriptions or asynchronous work, removal and recreation do not leave handlers, timers, stale results, or duplicate updates.
7. Keyboard behavior, accessible names, host-theme layout, and related console/network results are checked where browser tools are available.

Report executed checks separately from checks still requiring a browser or manual confirmation. For a narrow or display-only component, omit irrelevant features and tests rather than manufacturing them.

## Example short prompts

- “Create a component for selecting a time interval. Its value is an object with start and end times; support bounds, disabled state, and a callback on user change.”
- “Create a reusable status indicator bound to a string, with configurable labels and no editing.”
- “Create a multiple-selection component from a supplied item array, with search, a selection limit, and keyboard controls.”

Derive necessary hooks and methods from the requested behavior, confirm the APIs in the selected runtime, and document implementation assumptions. The user supplies the intended behavior, not a lifecycle checklist.

---

# jComponent 20: the published components

The 348 components of the catalogue of Total.js, each with what it does. Look here before you write a piece of interface by hand: when a component does what the screen needs, use it and do not write another one.

- Source: <https://github.com/totaljs/components> (`components/<name>/readme.md`), revision `f3ac05f7`. The page of each component is its readme, copied without changes.
- License: MIT, Copyright (c) Peter Širka. The notice is in [LICENSE](LICENSE).
- Update them with `node scripts/components.js`; do not edit them here.
- A live preview of each one is in <https://componentator.com>.

## How to use one

The first column is the name for `COMPONENTATOR()` and for `<ui-component>`:

```js
// definitions/init.js
ON('ready', function() {
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,input,validate,datagrid', true);
});
```

```html
<ui-component name="input" path="?.name" config="required:1">@(Name)</ui-component>
```

The page of the component has its configuration, its methods and an example.

|---|---|---|

# Total Icons: the names

The 600 icons of Total Icons, the icon font that the jComponent library loads. Use one of these names; a name that is not here draws nothing.

- Source: <https://github.com/totaljs/jComponent> (`spa.min@20.css`), revision `3fedd009`. License: MIT, Copyright (c) Peter Širka.
- Update the list with `node scripts/components.js`; do not edit it here.

## How to use an icon

The classes `ti` and `ti-` with the name:

```html
<i class="ti ti-check-circle"></i>
<button class="exec" data-exec="?/create"><i class="ti ti-plus-circle"></i>@(Create)</button>
```

In the metadata of a plugin and in the configuration of a component the icon is written with both classes:

```js
exports.icon = 'ti ti-check-circle';
```

# Total.js 5: what 0.0.20 adds

The stable version of `total5` on npm is `0.0.19` (`latest`). Version `0.0.20` is the beta (`npm install total5@beta`, `0.0.20-3` when this page was written). An application with `"total5": "latest"` does not have what is on this page until 0.0.20 is the stable version: use a feature of this page only in a project that depends on `total5@beta` or on `0.0.20` and later, and say so.

Every example here was run with `0.0.20-3`. The source of the list is the `changelog.txt` of the framework.

## Actions as MCP tools

`$mcp : true` in the file `config` opens the route `POST /$mcp/`. Every action with `mcp: true` is a tool there. The comment of a field is the description of the argument, and the `summary` of the action is the description of the tool.

```js
NEWACTION('Items|create', {
	name: 'Create an item',
	summary: 'Creates an item and returns it',
	mcp: true,
	input: '*name:String // The name of the item',
	action: function($, model) {
		$.callback({ name: model.name });
	}
});
```

- The tool is named `Items_create`: a name of a tool cannot have the pipe.
- A client lists the tools with `tools/list` and calls one with `tools/call` and the arguments `{ input: {}, query: {}, params: {} }`.
- By default every caller is accepted as an administrator. An application that other programs reach replaces `Total.mcp.auth = function($) { ... }` with its own check, as it does with `AUTH`.

## The cache of an action

`cache` keeps the answer of an action for the same request, so the action does not run again.

```js
NEWACTION('Items|list', {
	name: 'List of items',
	query: 'search:String',
	cache: { query: true, expire: '1 minute' },
	action: function($) {
		$.callback(items);
	}
});
```

`query: true`, `params: true` and `input: true` make one entry for each different value of them; `user: true` makes one for each user and `language: true` one for each language. `expire` is how long it is kept (`'5 minutes'` by default). Two calls with `?search=a` ran the action once; a call with `?search=b` ran it again.

## Two types for the fields: `JSON` and `IP`

```js
input: '*name:String, meta:JSON, address:IP'
```

- `JSON` accepts a text that is valid JSON. The value stays a text: the action parses it with `model.meta.parseJSON()`.
- `IP` accepts an IP address.
- A wrong value answers 400 with the name of the field, as the other types do.

## An answer with its own content type

```js
ROUTE('GET /export/', function($) {
	$.content('id;name\n1;Anna\n', 'text/csv');
});
```

`$.content(value, type)` answers with that text and that `content-type`. Without a type it is `application/octet-stream`.

## The environment of an action

A caller can name the environment of a call, and the action reads it in `$.env`:

```js
var response = await ACTION('Mail|send', model).env('test').promise();
```

```js
action: function($, model) {
	if ($.env === 'test') {
		$.callback({ sent: false });
		return;
	}
	// ...
}
```

## Tests: a command and fakes

`total5 test` runs the tests of the folder `tests` of the project (or of the current folder): it loads `tests/config` when it exists, then `tests/init.js`, then every other `.js` file. `total5 test name1 name2` runs only those files. A test file only needs `Test.push()`: the command loads the framework and runs them.

```js
// tests/orders.js
Test.push('orders', async function(next) {

	// The action that sends the email is replaced: the test does not send anything
	Test.fake('Mail|send', {
		name: 'Fake',
		action: function($) {
			$.callback({ sent: 'fake' });
		}
	});

	var response = await ACTION('Orders|close').promise();
	Test.print('closing an order sends the email', response.sent === 'fake' ? null : 'failed');

	Test.restore();
	next();
});
```

`Test.fake(name, definition)` takes the definition of an action, as `NEWACTION` does, and `Test.restore()` puts the real actions back.

## Smaller additions

| Addition | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Total.FsPromises` | The module `node:fs/promises`, as `Total.Fs` is `node:fs` |
| `User` | A global class: `new User({ id: '1', name: 'Anna' })` copies the fields to the object |
| `U.validhost(host)` | `true` for a plain hostname or a canonical IP address: `example.com` and `127.0.0.1` are valid, `0x7f.0.0.1` is not |
| `U.tohost(host)` | The canonical form of a hostname (`EXAMPLE.com` is `example.com`, `bücher.de` is `xn--bcher-kva.de`), or an empty text when it is not valid |

## In the changelog and not tried here

- `QueryBuilder.autoqueryjson($, column, schema, [defsort], [maxlimit])`: `autoquery()` for the properties of a JSON column.
- `JSONSchema.toAIObject(name, [description])` and `JSONSchema.toAITool(name)`.
- `$.throw(err)` and `$.touch([url])` in actions and controllers.
- The fixes of `CRON()` with a step (`*/15`), of the mail attachments, of `AJAX()` with XML and the hardening of hostnames.

## A problem found in 0.0.20-3

`$.invalidsafe(msg, err)` in an action throws `ReferenceError: path is not defined` and the request ends in a timeout. Use `$.invalid(msg)` and log the error apart until a later version fixes it.

question: How do I start a new Total.js 5 application?
question_es: ¿Cómo empiezo una aplicación nueva con Total.js 5?
---

# How do I start a new Total.js 5 application?

A Total.js 5 application is a folder with three files and the folders it needs:

```
index.js        the official start script, whole and unchanged
config          the settings, one "key : value" per line
package.json    "total5" is the dependency
controllers/    the routes
schemas/        the actions
definitions/    what runs at the start: AUTH, schedules, shared state
views/          the pages, when it has pages
public/         the static files
```

```json
{
	"name": "myapp",
	"version": "1.0.0",
	"main": "index.js",
	"dependencies": {
		"total5": "latest"
	},
	"scripts": {
		"start": "node index.js 8000"
	}
}
```

```text
name              : My application
```

`index.js` is always the official start script of the framework: copy it from [project structure](../conventions/general/project-structure.md), do not write a shorter one. Then `npm install` and `node index.js 8000`.

The settings are in the file `config`, not in `config.json` and not in environment variables. The smallest complete examples are [`apps/website`](../apps/website) (pages) and [`apps/contacts`](../apps/contacts) (an API).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/routes-and-actions.md

---
question: Where do the routes and the logic of an API go?
question_es: ¿Dónde van las rutas y la lógica de una API?
---

# Where do the routes and the logic of an API go?

The logic is an action, in a file of `schemas/`. The route is one line in a file of `controllers/` and points to the action. The name of an action has a pipe: `Collection|verb`.

```js
// schemas/contacts.js
NEWACTION('Contacts|create', {
	name: 'Create a contact',
	input: '*name:String, email:Email',
	action: async function($, model) {
		model.id = UID();
		model.dtcreated = NOW;
		await DATA.insert('nosql/tbl_contact', model).promise($);
		$.success(model.id);
	}
});
```

```js
// controllers/api.js
exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +contacts_create    --> Contacts|create');
};
```

- `input` is the body, `params` the parameters of the address (`{id}`) and `query` the query string. A `*` makes a field required; a wrong value answers 400 with the name of the field.
- The request is a `POST` to `/api/` with `{ "schema": "contacts_create", "data": { ... } }`.
- The first `+` of the route asks for a signed in user; the `+` before the name says that the request has a body, and a `-` that it has none.
- In an application with plugins the routes are in the `index.js` of the plugin. They are never declared inside the action in a new application.

See [`apps/contacts`](../apps/contacts) and [actions](../conventions/backend/actions.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/plugins-or-not.md

---
question: Should my application use plugins?
question_es: ¿Debe mi aplicación usar plugins?
---

# Should my application use plugins?

Use plugins when the application has screens to manage data and will grow by features: each feature is a folder in `plugins/` with its routes, its actions, its screen and its form, and adding one does not touch the rest.

Do not use plugins for a small API with one or two collections, or for a website with a few pages: `controllers/`, `schemas/` and `views/` are enough.

| The application | Shape | Example |
|---|---|---|
| A small API | No plugins: `controllers/` and `schemas/` | [`apps/contacts`](../apps/contacts) |
| Public pages | No plugins: `controllers/` and `views/` | [`apps/website`](../apps/website) |
| Screens to manage data, more features later | Plugins | [`apps/board`](../apps/board) |

```
plugins/tasks/
	index.js              the name, the icon, the position in the menu and the routes
	schemas/tasks.js      the actions
	public/index.html     the screen
	public/form.html      the form
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/which-storage.md

---
question: Where do I keep the data of a Total.js 5 application?
question_es: ¿Dónde guardo los datos de una aplicación Total.js 5?
---

# Where do I keep the data of a Total.js 5 application?

It depends on what the data is:

| The data | Use |
|---|---|
| The records of the application (contacts, tasks, orders) | `DATA` with QueryBuilder: `DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact')` on the embedded NoSQL database |
| An embedded store that will never be SQL (a log, a queue) | `NOSQL('name')` |
| A small object that is kept by itself (settings, counters) | `MEMORIZE('name')` |
| Files | `FILESTORAGE('name')` |

```js
var items = await DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);
var item = await DATA.read('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
await DATA.insert('nosql/tbl_contact', model).promise($);
await DATA.modify('nosql/tbl_contact', model).id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
await DATA.remove('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
```

The embedded database needs no server, no definition and no dependency: the file is `databases/tbl_contact.nosql`. Name the tables and the fields as in SQL from the start (`tbl_contact`, `isdone`, `dtcreated`), so that the application can move to PostgreSQL later.

Examples: [`apps/contacts`](../apps/contacts) (`DATA`), [`apps/files`](../apps/files) (`FILESTORAGE`), [`apps/monitor`](../apps/monitor) (`MEMORIZE`). The page: [storage](../conventions/backend/storage-and-integrations.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/move-to-postgresql.md

---
question: How do I move an application from the embedded database to PostgreSQL?
question_es: ¿Cómo paso una aplicación de la base de datos embebida a PostgreSQL?
---

# How do I move an application from the embedded database to PostgreSQL?

An application that uses `DATA` from the start changes four things, and no query is written again:

1. Add the adapter to `package.json`: `"querybuilderpg": "latest"`.
2. Add the connection to `config`: `database : postgresql://user:password@localhost/myapp`.
3. Add the definition of the database:

```js
// definitions/db.js
require('querybuilderpg').init('default', CONF.database, 1, ERROR('PostgreSQL'));
```

4. Take the prefix `nosql/` away from the table names:

```js
// before
var items = await DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);

// after
var items = await DATA.find('tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);
```

The tables must exist in PostgreSQL: write them in `database.sql`, with the same names the application already used.

[`apps/contacts`](../apps/contacts) and [`apps/contacts-postgresql`](../apps/contacts-postgresql) are the same application before and after; a test checks that their actions differ only in that prefix.

---
question: How do I protect an API with a token?
question_es: ¿Cómo protejo una API con un token?
---

# How do I protect an API with a token?

One `AUTH` in `definitions/auth.js` decides who each request is. A route that starts with `+` is only for a request that `AUTH` accepted.

```js
// definitions/auth.js
const BOT = { id: 'bot', name: 'Bot', sa: true };

AUTH(function($) {

	var token = $.headers['x-token'];

	if (!token) {
		$.invalid();
		return;
	}

	// Too many wrong tokens from the same client
	if (BLOCKED($, 10)) {
		$.invalid();
		return;
	}

	if (token === CONF.token) {
		BLOCKED($, -1);
		$.success(BOT);
	} else
		$.invalid();
});
```

```js
ROUTE('+API    ?    -contacts    --> Contacts|list');
```

The token is a setting of the file `config` (`token : ...`), read with `CONF.token`. A request without it, or with a wrong one, is answered with 401. Inside an action the user is `$.user`.

See [`apps/contacts`](../apps/contacts) and [routes and authentication](../conventions/backend/routes-and-auth.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/upload-files.md

---
question: How do I upload and download files?
question_es: ¿Cómo subo y descargo archivos?
---

# How do I upload and download files?

The upload is a `POST` route with `@upload` and a size limit; the files go to `FILESTORAGE`; the download is a `FILE` route.

```js
// controllers/api.js
ROUTE('+POST   /upload/    @upload <5MB    --> Files|upload');
ROUTE('FILE /download/*.*', download);

function download($) {
	var name = $.split[1];
	var opt = {};
	opt.id = name.substring(0, name.lastIndexOf('.'));
	opt.download = $.query.download === '1';
	FILESTORAGE('files').http($, opt);
}
```

```js
// schemas/files.js
NEWACTION('Files|upload', {
	name: 'Upload files',
	action: async function($) {
		var response = [];
		for (var i = 0; i < $.files.length; i++) {
			var meta = await $.files[i].fs('files', UID());
			meta.url = '/download/{0}.{1}'.format(meta.id, meta.ext);
			response.push(meta);
		}
		$.callback(response);
	}
});
```

`meta` has `id`, `name`, `size`, `ext`, `type` and `date`. A request over the limit is answered with 431. `FILESTORAGE('files').browse()` lists the files and `.remove(id, callback)` removes one.

The complete application: [`apps/files`](../apps/files).

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/websocket.md

---
question: How do I use a WebSocket?
question_es: ¿Cómo uso un WebSocket?
---

# How do I use a WebSocket?

A WebSocket is a route with the method `SOCKET`. Its function receives the socket of the route once; the events receive each connection.

```js
// controllers/default.js
exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('SOCKET /chat/', socket);
};

function socket($) {

	$.on('open', function(client) {
		client.send({ TYPE: 'hello' });        // to this connection
	});

	$.on('message', function(client, message) {
		$.send(message);                       // to everybody
	});

	$.on('close', function(client) {
	});
}
```

Messages are objects, sent and received as JSON; give each one a `TYPE`. `client.query` is the query of the address the browser connected to, and `$.connections` has the open connections. Check what the browser sends before using it.

In the browser, with jComponent 20:

```html
<ui-component name="websocket" config="url:/chat/"></ui-component>
```

```js
ON('message', function(msg) {
	// msg is the object the server sent
});

SETTER('websocket/send', { TYPE: 'message', text: 'Hello' });
```

Do not use `socket.io` or the package `ws`. The complete application: [`apps/chat`](../apps/chat).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/scheduled-work.md

---
question: How do I run something on a schedule?
question_es: ¿Cómo ejecuto algo de forma programada?
---

# How do I run something on a schedule?

In a file of `definitions/`. `ON('service')` is for "every N minutes" and `CRON` for a time of the day or of the week.

```js
// definitions/jobs.js

// The framework emits "service" every minute, with the number of minutes since the start
ON('service', function(counter) {
	if (counter % 5 === 0)
		ACTION('Sites|check').callback(ERROR('Sites|check'));
});

// Every day at midnight: minute hour day month weekday
CRON('0 0 * * *', function() {
	// ...
});
```

Put the work in an action and let the schedule only call it: the API can call it too, and it can be tested without waiting.

Write the minutes of a `CRON` as a list (`0,15,30,45 * * * *`). The step form (`*/15 * * * *`) runs every minute in Total.js 5 0.0.19; it works as a step from 0.0.20.

Do not use `setInterval` or a package for schedules. The complete application: [`apps/monitor`](../apps/monitor).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/pages.md

---
question: How do I make a page with a layout?
question_es: ¿Cómo hago una página con un layout?
---

# How do I make a page with a layout?

A route calls a function, and the function renders a view of `views/` with its data. The view goes inside `views/layout.html`, where `@{body}` is.

```js
// controllers/default.js
exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('GET /products/{id}/', product);
};

function product($) {
	var item = MAIN.products.findItem('id', $.params.id);
	if (!item) {
		$.fallback(404);
		return;
	}
	$.view('product', item);
}
```

```html
<!-- views/product.html -->
@{title(model.name)}

<h1>@{model.name}</h1>
<p>@{model.price.format(2)} EUR</p>
```

```html
<!-- views/layout.html -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<meta charset="utf-8" />
	@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.css')}
</head>
<body>
	@{body}
</body>
</html>
```

`@{title()}` sets the title (the framework adds the name of the application), `@{import()}` writes it and loads `public/css/default.css`, `@(Text)` marks a text for translation and `$.fallback(404)` answers with the page 404. Do not use `res.render`, `ejs` or `pug`.

The complete application: [`apps/website`](../apps/website).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/test-an-application.md

---
question: How do I test a Total.js 5 application?
question_es: ¿Cómo pruebo una aplicación Total.js 5?
---

# How do I test a Total.js 5 application?

With the test library of the framework, in a `test.js` that starts the application and calls it as a client does.

```js
require('total5');
require('total5/test');

Test.push('contacts', async function(next) {
	// call() is a function of the test that sends the request to the application, as the api() of apps/contacts/test.js
	var response = await call('contacts_create', { name: 'Anna' });
	Test.print('create answers with the id', response.success === true ? null : 'failed');
	next();
});

Test.run();
```

`Test.print(message, error)` fails when the second argument is not empty. Run it with `node test.js`.

What the tests of this repository do, and why:

- They copy the application to a disposable folder and start it there with `node index.js <port>`, so the data of the application is never touched.
- They wait until the application answers before the first check: the server answers before its routes are loaded.
- They check the errors too: without the token, with a wrong field, with an id that does not exist.
- A test that needs a database server uses one only for tests, and says `SKIPPED` when it is not there.

Every application of [`apps/`](../apps) has a `test.js` to copy from. The page: [testing](../conventions/general/testing.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/javascript-style.md

---
question: Which JavaScript style does Total.js 5 code use?
question_es: ¿Qué estilo de JavaScript usa el código de Total.js 5?
---

# Which JavaScript style does Total.js 5 code use?

ES5 first, and the functions of the framework before any other.

```js
// good
var item = items.findItem('id', id);
var text = 'Hello {0}'.format(name);

// avoid
const item = items.find(m => m.id === id);
const text = `Hello ${name}`;
```

- `var` and `function`; no arrow functions and no template literals. `const` or `let` only where the code needs it, as a constant at the top of a file.
- `async` / `await` where the code waits for the database: `await DATA.find(...).promise($)`.
- The prototypes of Total.js before your own helper: `findItem`, `format`, `parseJSON`, `slug`, `isEmail`.
- No `require()` of a module of Node.js in the application: `Total.Fs`, `Total.Path`, `Total.Crypto`, `Total.Os`.
- Tabs, semicolons, `'` for short texts, file names in lowercase with `-`.
- `index.js` is the one exception: it is the official start script and keeps its own style.

The page: [JavaScript style](../conventions/general/javascript-style.md).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/not-express.md

---
question: Is Total.js like Express? Which packages do I need?
question_es: ¿Total.js es como Express? ¿Qué paquetes necesito?
---

# Is Total.js like Express? Which packages do I need?

No. Total.js 5 is one package, `total5`, and it already has what an Express application adds with packages. An application does not install them and does not write `app.get()`.

| Instead of | Total.js 5 has |
|---|---|
| `express`, `app.get('/', ...)` | `ROUTE('GET /', fn)` in `controllers/` |
| `body-parser`, `joi` | `input` of `NEWACTION`: the body is parsed and checked |
| `dotenv`, `process.env` | the file `config` and `CONF` |
| `ejs`, `pug` | the views of `views/` with `@{...}` |
| `multer` | a route with `@upload` and `$.files` |
| `socket.io`, `ws` | `ROUTE('SOCKET /', fn)` |
| `node-cron`, `setInterval` | `CRON()` and `ON('service')` |
| `axios`, `node-fetch` | `RESTBuilder` |
| `uuid` | `UID()` |
| a database for a small application | the embedded NoSQL database through `DATA` |

The only other dependency of the applications of this repository is `querybuilderpg`, for PostgreSQL.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/answers/versions.md

---
question: Which version of Total.js 5 should I use, and what does the beta add?
question_es: ¿Qué versión de Total.js 5 debo usar y qué añade la beta?
---

# Which version of Total.js 5 should I use, and what does the beta add?

Use `"total5": "latest"` in `package.json`: it is the stable version. When this was written the stable version was `0.0.19` and the beta was `0.0.20`; `npm view total5 dist-tags` says which they are today.

Total.js 5 is the current framework. Total.js 4 (`total4`) is the previous one and its code is not the same: do not mix them.

What 0.0.20 adds is in [reference](../reference/total5-0.0.20.md): actions as MCP tools, the cache of an action, the field types `JSON` and `IP`, `$.content()`, `total5 test` and fakes for tests. Use one of those only in a project that depends on `total5@beta` or on 0.0.20 and later, and say which version it needs.

When you are not sure that a function exists in the version of the project, say so and check it in the source of the framework instead of guessing.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/application.md

# The application: questions and answers

## Which folders does a Total.js 5 application have?

The framework loads each folder by its name:

```
index.js            the official start script
config              settings, one "key : value" per line
package.json        "total5" is the dependency
controllers/        routes
definitions/        auth.js, init.js, func.js, db.js: loaded at start
schemas/            actions
modules/            integrations with other systems
plugins/<name>/     a feature with its server part and its screen
views/              layout and pages
public/             static files for the browser
```

A small API needs only `index.js`, `config`, `package.json`, `controllers/`, `schemas/` and `definitions/`.

## What goes in index.js?

The official start script of Total.js 5, whole and unchanged: `helpers/index.js` of the framework. Its heart is this, and the commented options of the official file stay in it:

```js
require('total5');

const options = {};

options.release = process.argv.includes('--release');
options.servicemode = process.argv.includes('--service') || process.argv.includes('--servicemode');

Total.run(options);
```

Do not write a shorter one by hand and do not restyle it: it is the one file that keeps its own style.

## How do I start a Total.js 5 application?

```
npm install
node index.js 8000
```

The number is the port. Add `--release` for release mode: `node index.js 8000 --release`.

## What does package.json need?

Only `total5`. The framework has the server, the routes, the templates, the database builder and the tests inside:

```json
{
	"name": "contacts",
	"version": "1.0.0",
	"private": true,
	"dependencies": {
		"total5": "latest"
	}
}
```

## How is the config file written?

It is a plain file named `config`, without an extension, with one `key : value` per line. A line that starts with `//` is a comment:

```
name              : Contacts

// The requests of the API must send this value in the header "x-token"
token             : change-this-token
```

The code reads a value with `CONF.token`. It is not JSON and it is not a `.env` file.

## Where do I read a setting in the code?

In `CONF`, with the key of the file `config`:

```js
if (token === CONF.token)
	$.success(BOT);
```

The settings that belong to the framework start with `$`, as `$api`. Keys and addresses of databases stay out of the repository.

## Where do shared helper functions go?

In `definitions/func.js`, as functions of `FUNC`, named in lowercase without separators:

```js
// definitions/func.js
FUNC.refreshtags = async function() {
	REPO.tags = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').promise();
};
```

Actions and controllers call `FUNC.refreshtags()`.

## Where do I keep state in memory?

In `MAIN`, the object of the application, filled in a file of `definitions/`:

```js
// definitions/db.js
MAIN.products = [
	{ id: 'bread', name: 'Sourdough bread', price: 4.5 }
];
```

`REPO` holds cached lookups that the interface also needs. Do not create new globals.

## Where does the work of the start go?

In `ON('ready', ...)` of `definitions/init.js`: it runs when the application is up.

```js
// definitions/init.js
ON('ready', function() {
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,form,validate', true);
});
```

## How do I name files and folders?

All lowercase, words separated by `-`, never `_`: `search-results.html`. Static files go by type in `public/`: `/img/`, `/js/`, `/css/`, `/fonts/`. One plugin per feature, named after it: `plugins/redirects`.

## What is a module and how do I use it?

A file of `modules/` is an integration with another system or a service of its own. The framework loads it and registers its exports in `MODS`, under the name of the file:

```js
var data = MODS.visitors.today();
```

Do not load an application module with `require(PATH.root('modules/...'))`. A name with a dash uses brackets: `MODS['knowledge-source']`.

## Should a new application use plugins?

It depends on the project. An application that will grow by features is made with plugins: each feature is a folder `plugins/<name>/` with its routes, its actions and its screen. A small service with one or two collections does not need them: `controllers/` and `schemas/` are enough.

## Do I need Express or other packages?

No. Total.js 5 is not built on Express and does not use its middleware. Routes, actions, validation, templates, WebSocket, the database builder and the tests are in `total5`. The only other package a common application adds is the adapter of its database, as `querybuilderpg` for PostgreSQL.

## Which version of Total.js 5 do I install?

`"total5": "latest"` in `package.json` is the stable version. The beta is `npm install total5@beta`. `npm view total5 dist-tags` says which versions they are today. Total.js 4 (`total4`) is the previous framework and its code is not the same.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/actions.md

# Actions: questions and answers

## What is an action?

One unit of server logic: a name, the input it accepts, who may call it, and a function. It is defined with `NEWACTION` in a file of `schemas/`:

```js
NEWACTION('Contacts|create', {
	name: 'Create a contact',
	input: '*name:String, email:Email, phone:Phone',
	action: async function($, model) {
		model.id = UID();
		model.dtcreated = NOW;
		await DATA.insert('nosql/tbl_contact', model).promise($);
		$.success(model.id);
	}
});
```

## How do I name an action?

`Collection|verb`: the collection in plural with a capital letter, a pipe, and the verb. `Tickets|list`, `Groups|create`, `Users|remove`. Never `/` between the parts.

```js
NEWACTION('Tickets|list', {
	name: 'List of tickets',
	action: function($) {
		DATA.find('nosql/tbl_ticket').callback($);
	}
});
```

## Which verbs do actions use?

| Verb | Does |
|---|---|
| `list` | returns a collection |
| `read` | returns one record |
| `create` | inserts and answers with the new id |
| `update` | modifies one record |
| `save` | creates or updates by `id` |
| `remove` | deletes one record |

## Where do I put the actions?

In `schemas/`, one file per collection: `schemas/contacts.js`. In an application with plugins, in `plugins/<name>/schemas/`. The routes that call them go in `controllers/` or in the `index.js` of the plugin.

## How do I declare the input of an action?

With a text in `input`: the fields separated by commas, `*` before a required field and the type after `:`.

```js
input: '*name:String, email:Email, phone:Phone, isactive:Boolean, tags:[String]'
```

The body arrives validated as the second argument of the function: `action: function($, model)`.

## Which types can a field have?

`String`, `String(100)` with a maximum length, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Date`, `UID`, `Email`, `Phone`, `URL`, `Color`, `Icon`, and a list with brackets: `[String]`. A wrong value answers 400 with the name of the field.

## How do I read the id of the address?

Declare it in `params` and read it in `$.params`:

```js
NEWACTION('Contacts|read', {
	name: 'Read a contact',
	params: '*id:UID',
	action: async function($) {
		var item = await DATA.read('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
		$.callback(item);
	}
});
```

The route has `{id}` in its address: `ROUTE('+API ? -contacts_read/{id} --> Contacts|read')`.

## How do I read the query string in an action?

Declare it in `query` and read it in `$.query`:

```js
NEWACTION('Items|list', {
	name: 'List of items',
	query: 'search:String',
	action: function($) {
		$.callback($.query.search);
	}
});
```

## How does an action answer?

| Call | Use |
|---|---|
| `$.callback(data)` | returns data: a record, a list |
| `$.success()` or `$.success(id)` | the answer of success, with a value if you pass one |
| `$.invalid(404)` | an error with that HTTP status |
| `$.invalid('@(Text for the user)')` | a validation or business error |

Answer once on each path, and `return` after an early answer.

## How do I answer that a record does not exist?

`$.invalid(404)`. With `DATA`, `.error(404)` does it when the query finds nothing:

```js
if (!item) {
	$.invalid(404);
	return;
}
```

```js
var item = await DATA.read('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
```

## How do I answer with an error message for the user?

`$.invalid('@(text)')`. The `@(...)` marks the text for translation:

```js
if (MAIN.monitor.sites.findItem('url', model.url)) {
	$.invalid('@(The website is already in the list)');
	return;
}
```

## How do I restrict an action to some users?

With `permissions` or `user: true` in the action. The `+` of the route asks for a logged-in user; the check of the action also protects a call that does not come from that route.

```js
NEWACTION('Redirects|save', {
	name: 'Save redirect',
	input: 'id,*url,*target,permanent:Boolean',
	permissions: 'redirects,admin',
	action: function($, model) {
		$.success();
	}
});
```

## How do I reuse the fields of an input?

With a named schema and `@`:

```js
NEWSCHEMA('@Group', '*name,color:Color,icon:Icon,reference,permissions:[String]');

NEWACTION('Groups|create', {
	name: 'Create group',
	input: '@Group',
	action: function($, model) {
		$.success();
	}
});
```

## How do I call one action from another?

`$.action('Name').promise()` inside an action, and `ACTION('Name', model)` outside a request:

```js
var types = await $.action('Items|types').promise();
```

```js
ACTION('Sites|check').callback(ERROR('Sites|check'));
```

## Why is my action async?

Because it waits for the database. Pass `$` to `.promise($)`: an error of the query then answers the request by itself.

```js
action: async function($) {
	var item = await DATA.read('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
	$.callback(item);
}
```

## Does every action need a name?

Yes: `name` is a short text for people ("Save redirect"). Logs and tools use it. The first argument of `NEWACTION` is its identifier (`Redirects|save`).

## Why does my required list reject an empty list?

A field `*tags:[String]` is required, and an empty list counts as missing. If an empty list is valid, take the `*` away: `tags:[String]`.

## Why is my Boolean false when the field was not sent?

A `Boolean` that is absent is `false`. When the absence must mean "unchanged", declare the action with `partial: true`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/routes.md

# Routes and authentication: questions and answers

## Where do the routes go?

In `exports.install` of a file of `controllers/`, or of the `index.js` of a plugin. One line per route:

```js
// controllers/api.js
exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -contacts                --> Contacts|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -contacts_read/{id}      --> Contacts|read');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +contacts_create         --> Contacts|create');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +contacts_update/{id}    --> Contacts|update');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -contacts_remove/{id}    --> Contacts|remove');
};
```

## How do I read an API route?

```js
ROUTE('+API    ?    +tickets_create    --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
```

- The first `+` is "only for logged-in users". Without it the route is public.
- `?` is the address of the API: `/api/` by default.
- `+tickets_create` is the name of the endpoint; its `+` says the request has a body, and `-` says it has none.
- After `-->` goes the action.
- The number is the maximum size of the body in bytes.

## How does a client call an API route?

With a `POST` to the address of the API (`/api/`), with the name of the endpoint in `schema` and the body in `data`:

```
POST /api/
x-token: change-this-token
content-type: application/json

{ "schema": "contacts_create", "data": { "name": "Anna" } }
```

An endpoint with a parameter carries it in the name: `"schema": "contacts_read/ID"`.

## How do I name an endpoint?

In lowercase with `_`: `tickets_create`, `users_remove/{id}`. Use `-` before the name for reads and removals, and `+` for creates and updates. `{id}` fills `$.params.id`.

## How do I make a route that returns a page?

A `GET` route with a function that receives `$`:

```js
exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('GET /', home);
	ROUTE('GET /products/{id}/', product);
};

function home($) {
	$.view('index');
}
```

## How do I answer JSON from a route function?

With `$.json(data)`. In a route function `$.callback(err, value)` takes the error first, so it is not the call of an action:

```js
ROUTE('GET /status/', function($) {
	$.json({ ok: true });
});
```

## How do I make a public route?

Leave out the `+` before the method. `ROUTE('POST /notify/', notify)` is public; `ROUTE('+GET /setup/', setup)` is only for logged-in users.

## How does the application know who the request is from?

With one `AUTH` in `definitions/auth.js`. It calls `$.success(user)` or `$.invalid()`:

```js
const BOT = { id: 'bot', name: 'Bot', sa: true };

AUTH(function($) {
	var token = $.headers['x-token'];
	if (token && token === CONF.token)
		$.success(BOT);
	else
		$.invalid();
});
```

Every route with `+` then needs that user.

## How do I protect an API with a token?

Put the token in `config`, check the header in `AUTH` and mark the routes with `+`:

```js
AUTH(function($) {

	var token = $.headers['x-token'];

	if (!token) {
		$.invalid();
		return;
	}

	if (BLOCKED($, 10)) {
		$.invalid();
		return;
	}

	if (token === CONF.token) {
		BLOCKED($, -1);
		$.success(BOT);
	} else
		$.invalid();
});
```

## How do I limit wrong login tries?

With `BLOCKED($, limit)`: it counts the tries of each client and returns `true` once the limit is passed. `BLOCKED($, -1)` forgets them after a good login.

```js
if (BLOCKED($, 10)) {
	$.invalid();
	return;
}
```

## What does the user object look like?

A small object: `{ id, name, sa, permissions }`. `sa` marks a super administrator. `AUTH` gives it with `$.success(user)` and actions read it in `$.user`.

## How do I give a route a larger body limit?

With the size in bytes as the second argument of `ROUTE`:

```js
ROUTE('+API    ?    +tickets_create    --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
```

An upload says its size in the route itself: `<5MB`.

## Can an action declare its own route?

Yes: `route: '+API ?'` in `NEWACTION` registers the endpoint. In a new application write the routes in `controllers/` or in the `index.js` of the plugin, so that all of them are read in one place, and do not declare the same route twice.

## Is $.ip safe for a security limit?

No. `$.ip` is the first value of the header `X-Forwarded-For`, which a client can write. For a security limit use `$.req.socket.remoteAddress`, or trust the header only behind your own proxy.

## How do I answer 404 from a page?

With `$.fallback(404)`: it is the page 404 of the framework, as for an address without a route.

```js
function product($) {
	var item = MAIN.products.findItem('id', $.params.id);
	if (!item) {
		$.fallback(404);
		return;
	}
	$.view('product', item);
}
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/data.md

# Data with DATA: questions and answers

## Where do I keep the records of a new application?

In the embedded NoSQL database, through `DATA`, with the prefix `nosql/` before the name of the table. It needs no server, no definition and no dependency:

```js
var items = await DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);
```

The file is `databases/tbl_contact.nosql`.

## How do I list records?

```js
NEWACTION('Contacts|list', {
	name: 'List of contacts',
	action: async function($) {
		var items = await DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);
		$.callback(items);
	}
});
```

## How do I read one record?

`DATA.read()` with `.id()`. `.error(404)` answers 404 when it does not exist:

```js
var item = await DATA.read('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
```

## How do I insert a record?

Fill the id with `UID()` and the date with `NOW` in the action:

```js
model.id = UID();
model.dtcreated = NOW;
await DATA.insert('nosql/tbl_contact', model).promise($);
$.success(model.id);
```

## How do I update a record?

```js
model.dtupdated = NOW;
await DATA.modify('nosql/tbl_contact', model).id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
$.success($.params.id);
```

## How do I remove a record?

```js
await DATA.remove('nosql/tbl_contact').id($.params.id).error(404).promise($);
$.success($.params.id);
```

## How do I make a unique id?

`UID()`. It is a function of the framework: no package and no `require`.

```js
model.id = UID();
```

## How do I filter a query?

With conditions on the builder: `where(field, value)`, `in(field, array)`, `notin(field, array)`, `search(field, keyword)`.

```js
var items = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').where('folderid', id).promise($);
```

## How do I choose the fields a query returns?

`.fields('a,b')`. Name them; do not read everything:

```js
var item = await DATA.read('tbl_user').fields('id,name').id(params.id).error('@(User not found)').promise($);
```

## How do I make a list with paging, sorting and filters from the query string?

With `autoquery`: it reads `?page=`, `limit`, `sort` and the fields you allow, with a default sort and a maximum page size.

```js
NEWACTION('Groups|list', {
	name: 'List of groups',
	action: function($) {
		DATA.find('op.view_group').autoquery($.query, 'id:UID,name,color,icon,users:Number,dtcreated:Date,dtupdated:Date', 'dtcreated_desc', 100).callback($);
	}
});
```

## How do I connect the application to PostgreSQL?

Add the package `querybuilderpg`, put the address of the database in `config` and write one definition:

```js
// definitions/db.js
require('querybuilderpg').init('default', CONF.database, 1, ERROR('PostgreSQL'));
```

The queries are the same `DATA` calls, with the name of the table without a prefix: `DATA.find('tbl_contact')`.

## How do I move from the embedded database to PostgreSQL?

Take the prefix `nosql/` away from the table names, add the definition of `querybuilderpg` and create the tables with `database.sql`. The queries do not change:

```js
// before
var items = await DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);

// after
var items = await DATA.find('tbl_contact').sort('name').promise($);
```

## How do I run raw SQL?

`DATA.query()` with parameters:

```js
await DATA.query('UPDATE tbl_ticket SET worked=worked+1 WHERE id=$1', [id]).promise($);
```

Prefer parameters (`$1`). When a value must go into the text, escape it with `PG_ESCAPE(value)`. Never concatenate what a user sent.

## How do I answer with success after a write without async?

`.callback($.done(id))` answers with the success of the application and that value:

```js
DATA.remove('tbl_tag').id($.params.id).error(404).callback($.done($.params.id));
```

`.callback($)` answers with the raw result of the query instead.

## How do I use DATA outside a request?

`.promise()` without `$`, with its own error handling, or a callback with the error first:

```js
FUNC.refreshtags = async function() {
	REPO.tags = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').promise();
};
```

## How do I search by text in several fields?

With `or` and `search`:

```js
builder.or(function(b) {
	b.search('name', text);
	b.search('email', text);
});
```

## Do I need to set up QueryBuilder for the embedded database?

No. QueryBuilder comes loaded with Total.js 5 and the prefix `nosql/` sends the query to the embedded database. Only a database server needs its adapter, as `querybuilderpg`.

## How do I name tables and fields in the embedded database?

As in SQL from the first day, so the application can move to PostgreSQL later: tables `tbl_contact`, dates `dtcreated` and `dtupdated`, flags `isdone`, a foreign key as the table plus `id` (`userid`).

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/storage.md

# Storage and files: questions and answers

## Which storage do I choose for a new application?

By what the data is:

| The data | Use |
|---|---|
| The records of the application (contacts, tasks, orders) | `DATA` on the embedded database: `DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact')` |
| An embedded store that will never be SQL (a log, a queue) | `NOSQL('name')` |
| A small object that is kept by itself (settings, counters) | `MEMORIZE('name')` |
| Files | `FILESTORAGE('name')` |

## How do I keep a small object between restarts without a database?

With `MEMORIZE`: the framework keeps the object in a file by itself.

```js
// definitions/db.js
MAIN.monitor = MEMORIZE('monitor', 1000);

if (!MAIN.monitor.sites)
	MAIN.monitor.sites = [];
```

The second argument is the delay of the save in milliseconds. After a change call `MAIN.monitor.save()`.

## How do I save a change of a MEMORIZE object?

Change the object and call its `save()`:

```js
MAIN.monitor.sites.push(model);
MAIN.monitor.save();
$.success(model.id);
```

## When do I use NOSQL() directly?

For an embedded store that will never be SQL: a log, a queue, a cache on disk. The records of the application go through `DATA` with the prefix `nosql/`, which reads the same file and lets the application move to PostgreSQL later.

```js
NOSQL('logs').insert({ id: UID(), message: 'Started', dtcreated: NOW });
```

## How do I receive an uploaded file?

A `POST` route with `@upload` and the maximum size, and an action that reads `$.files`:

```js
ROUTE('+POST   /upload/    @upload <5MB    --> Files|upload');
```

```js
NEWACTION('Files|upload', {
	name: 'Upload files',
	action: async function($) {

		if (!$.files.length) {
			$.invalid('@(No file was sent)');
			return;
		}

		var response = [];

		for (var i = 0; i < $.files.length; i++) {
			var meta = await $.files[i].fs('files', UID());
			response.push(meta);
		}

		$.callback(response);
	}
});
```

## Where are uploaded files kept?

In a `FILESTORAGE`. `$.files[i].fs('files', UID())` moves the uploaded file to the storage named `files` with a new id, and returns its metadata. The folder is `databases/fs-files`.

## How do I list the files of a storage?

```js
var items = await FILESTORAGE('files').browse().promise($);
```

Each item has its `id`, its name, its extension (`ext`) and its size.

## How do I send a stored file to the browser?

With a `FILE` route and the `http()` of the storage:

```js
ROUTE('FILE /download/*.*', download);

function download($) {
	var name = $.split[1];
	var opt = {};
	opt.id = name.substring(0, name.lastIndexOf('.'));
	opt.download = $.query.download === '1';
	FILESTORAGE('files').http($, opt);
}
```

## How do I remove a stored file?

```js
FILESTORAGE('files').remove($.params.id, function(err) {
	if (err)
		$.invalid(404);
	else
		$.success($.params.id);
});
```

## What happens when an upload is larger than the limit of the route?

The framework rejects the request with the status 431 and the action does not run. The limit is in the route: `@upload <5MB`.

## Should an existing application change its storage?

No. A feature keeps the model it already has: metadata in memory saved to a file, SQL through `DATA`, or a `MEMORIZE` object. Do not switch the storage during a cleanup.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/services.md

# Scheduled work, HTTP calls and WebSocket: questions and answers

## How do I run something every minute?

The framework emits `service` every minute, with the number of minutes since the start. No timer and no package:

```js
// definitions/init.js
ON('service', function(counter) {
	if (counter % 5 === 0)
		ACTION('Sites|check').callback(ERROR('Sites|check'));
});
```

`counter % 5 === 0` is every five minutes.

## How do I run something at a time of the day?

With `CRON` and the five fields of a cron line:

```js
// Every day at midnight
CRON('0 0 * * *', function() {
	MAIN.monitor.save();
});
```

In Total.js 5 0.0.19 a step (`*/5`) runs every minute; it is fixed in 0.0.20. For "every N minutes" use `ON('service')`.

## Should I use setInterval for repeated work?

No. Use `ON('service', function(counter) { ... })`: one listener for the application, with the count of minutes, instead of a timer of your own.

## How do I call another HTTP service?

With `RESTBuilder`, which is in the framework:

```js
var response = await RESTBuilder.GET(CONF.serviceurl).promise($);
```

Check the status and the shape of the answer before you answer with success.

## How do I send a POST with JSON to another service?

```js
RESTBuilder.POST(CONF.serviceurl, { name: 'Anna' }).header('x-token', CONF.servicetoken).callback(function(err, response) {
	if (err)
		$.invalid('@(The service did not answer)');
	else
		$.callback(response);
});
```

## How do I read the HTTP status of a remote answer?

With `exec`, which gives the output with its status:

```js
RESTBuilder.GET(site.url).timeout(CONF.timeout).exec(function(err, response, output) {
	site.status = output && output.status ? output.status : 0;
});
```

A request that takes longer than the timeout has the status 408, and an address where nothing listens has 0.

## How do I declare a WebSocket route?

With `SOCKET` in a controller. The function receives the controller of the room:

```js
exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('SOCKET /chat/', socket);
};

function socket($) {

	$.on('open', function(client) {
		client.send({ TYPE: 'hello' });
	});

	$.on('message', function(client, message) {
		$.send(message);
	});

	$.on('close', function(client) {
	});
}
```

## How do I send a WebSocket message to everybody or to one client?

`$.send(message)` sends it to every connection of the route, the sender too. `client.send(message)` sends it to one client. The messages are objects: the framework sends them as JSON.

## How do I go through the connections of a WebSocket route?

They are in `$.connections`:

```js
var names = [];
for (var key in $.connections) {
	var client = $.connections[key];
	client.name && names.push(client.name);
}
```

## How do I read the query string of a WebSocket connection?

In `client.query`, inside `open`:

```js
$.on('open', function(client) {
	var name = (client.query.name || '').trim().substring(0, 30);
	client.name = name;
});
```

## How do I close a WebSocket connection that is not allowed?

`client.close(code)`, a moment after `open`, when the connection is completely open:

```js
if (!name) {
	setTimeout(function(client) {
		client.close(4001);
	}, 500, client);
	return;
}
```

## How do I log an error of work that has no request?

With `ERROR('context')` as the callback: it writes the error with that name.

```js
ACTION('Sites|check').callback(ERROR('Sites|check'));
```

Use `NOOP` only for a result that you ignore on purpose.

## How do I go through a list with an asynchronous call, one after another?

With `wait` of the array:

```js
MAIN.monitor.sites.wait(function(site, next) {
	RESTBuilder.GET(site.url).exec(function(err, response, output) {
		site.status = output && output.status ? output.status : 0;
		next();
	});
}, function() {
	$.callback(MAIN.monitor.sites);
});
```

## How do I react to a change of the configuration?

With `ON('configure', ...)`. The part that changes the settings emits it with `EMIT('configure')`. Settings kept in a table are loaded with `LOADCONFIG(rows)`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/views.md

# Views and pages: questions and answers

## How do I render a page?

A route calls `$.view()` with the name of a file of `views/`:

```js
// controllers/default.js
exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('GET /', home);
};

function home($) {
	$.view('index');
}
```

```html
<!-- views/index.html -->
@{title(CONF.name)}

<h1>@(Fresh every morning)</h1>
```

## How do I pass data to a view?

As the second argument of `$.view()`. The view reads it as `model`:

```js
$.view('product', item);
```

```html
@{title(model.name)}

<h1>@{model.name}</h1>
<p>@{model.description}</p>
```

## How do I make a layout for all the pages?

`views/layout.html` is the layout of every view. `@{body}` is where the view goes:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<meta charset="utf-8" />
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
	@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.css')}
</head>
<body>
	<main>
		@{body}
	</main>
</body>
</html>
```

## How do I loop over a list in a view?

With `@{foreach}` and `@{end}`:

```html
<ul class="products">
@{foreach m in model}
	<li>
		<a href="/products/@{m.id}/">@{m.name}</a>
		<span>@{m.price.format(2)} EUR</span>
	</li>
@{end}
</ul>
```

## How do I write a condition in a view?

With `@{if}` and `@{fi}`:

```html
@{if model.price}
	<p class="price">@{model.price.format(2)} EUR</p>
@{fi}
```

## How do I set the title of a page?

With `@{title()}` at the top of the view. The layout prints it through `@{import('meta')}`, and the framework adds " - " and the name of the application after it:

```html
@{title('@(Products)')}
```

## How do I mark a text for translation?

Wrap it in `@(...)`, in views, in the HTML of plugins and in the messages of the server. The text in English is the key:

```html
<a href="/products/">@(Products)</a>
```

```js
$.invalid('@(The website is already in the list)');
```

The translations are in `resources/<language>.resource`.

## How do I read a setting in a view?

`@{CONF.name}`:

```html
<a href="/" class="logo">@{CONF.name}</a>
<a href="mailto:@{CONF.email}">@{CONF.email}</a>
```

## How do I use a view without the layout?

Put `@{layout('')}` at the top of the view. The shell of an application with jComponent is a view like that: a whole HTML document of its own.

## How do I load the CSS and JavaScript of the application in the layout?

With `@{import()}` in the `<head>`. The files are in `public/css/` and `public/js/`:

```html
@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.js + func.js', 'default.css', 'favicon.ico')}
```

## Is the syntax of the views the same as Tangular?

No. A view of `views/` uses `@{...}` and is rendered on the server. Tangular uses `{{ ... }}` and is for templates, mostly in the browser. Do not write one inside the other expecting the other engine.

## What are the two kinds of pages?

Public pages are views that a controller returns with `$.view('index')`. Application screens (an admin, a tool) are the HTML of plugins, mounted in a shell and driven by `PLUGIN` with jComponent.

## Why do I not see my change of a static file in release mode?

In release mode static files are served from memory: restart the application after changing them. The browser also keeps them: force a reload while testing.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/tangular.md

# Tangular templates: questions and answers

## What is Tangular?

The template engine of Total.js: text with `{{ ... }}` commands that is filled with a model. jComponent uses it in the browser for what a screen draws from data, and the framework has the same engine on the server.

```js
var html = Tangular.render('Hello {{ name }}!', { name: 'Anna' });
```

The result is `Hello Anna!`.

## How do I print a value in Tangular?

`{{ name }}`. The value is HTML-encoded, so the text of a user can be shown as it is. A property of an object is `{{ user.name }}`, and an expression works too: `{{ age + 1 }}`.

## How do I print a value without HTML encoding in Tangular?

With the helper `raw`:

```html
{{ html | raw }}
```

Use it only for HTML that the application made itself, never for text that a user wrote. `{{ !html }}` is not raw: `!` is the negation of JavaScript.

## How do I write a condition in Tangular?

`{{ if }}`, `{{ else if }}`, `{{ else }}` and `{{ fi }}`:

```html
{{ if age > 40 }}old{{ else if age > 30 }}middle{{ else }}young{{ fi }}
```

The condition is a JavaScript expression. It ends with `{{ fi }}`.

## How do I loop over a list in Tangular?

`{{ foreach m in items }}` and `{{ end }}`:

```html
{{ foreach m in items }}
<div class="item">{{ m.name }}</div>
{{ end }}
```

A loop ends with `{{ end }}` and a condition with `{{ fi }}`: they are not the same word.

## How do I get the position of an item in a Tangular loop?

`$index`, from 0:

```html
{{ foreach m in items }}{{ $index }}:{{ m.name }} {{ end }}
```

`{{ continue }}` goes to the next item and `{{ break }}` ends the loop.

## How do I format a number or a date in Tangular?

With the helper `format`:

```html
{{ price | format(2) }}
{{ date | format('yyyy-MM-dd') }}
```

`1234.5` becomes `1 234.50`, and the date becomes `2026-11-12`.

## How do I show a text when a value is empty in Tangular?

With `empty` or `def`:

```html
{{ name | empty('No name') }}
{{ nothing | def('nothing here') }}
```

`{{ name | empty }}` without a text writes `---`. A value that is `null` or does not exist is an empty text, not an error.

## How do I write a plural in Tangular?

With `pluralize` and four texts: for zero, one, a few and many. `#` is the number:

```html
{{ count | pluralize('no items', '# item', '# items', '# items') }}
```

## How do I make my own Tangular helper?

```js
Thelpers.upper = function(value) {
	return Thelpers.encode((value || '').toUpperCase());
};
```

```html
{{ name | upper }}
```

The result of a helper is written without encoding: a helper that returns text of a user encodes it with `Thelpers.encode(value)`.

## How do I draw a list on a screen with a template?

With a `ui-bind` and `config="template"`. It draws its template every time its path changes, and inside the template the data is `value`:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.items" config="template" class="block">
	<script type="text/html">
		{{ foreach m in value }}
		<div class="item{{ if m.isdone }} done{{ fi }}">{{ m.name }}</div>
		{{ end }}
	</script>
</ui-bind>
```

Change the model and let the `ui-bind` draw; do not build the HTML by joining texts.

## How do I compile a template to use it many times?

```js
var template = Tangular.compile('Hello {{ name }}!');
var html = template({ name: 'Zoe' });
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/questions/interface.md

# The interface with jComponent 20: questions and answers

## What is a plugin?

A feature of an application: a folder with its server part and its screen, which the framework loads and the shell of the application mounts.

```
plugins/redirects/
	index.js              server: metadata and routes
	schemas/redirects.js  actions
	public/index.html     the screen
	public/form.html      the form that opens over the screen
```

## What goes in the index.js of a plugin?

Its icon, its name, its position in the menu, who sees it, and its routes:

```js
exports.icon = 'ti ti-check-circle';
exports.name = '@(Tasks)';
exports.position = 1;
exports.visible = function() {
	return true;
};

exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -tasks                   --> Tasks|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +tasks_save              --> Tasks|save');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -tasks_remove/{id}       --> Tasks|remove');
};
```

## How do I write the screen of a plugin?

HTML with a `<ui-plugin>` root and one `PLUGIN(function(exports) { ... })` block, in `public/index.html`:

```html
<ui-plugin class="CLASS">
	<button class="exec" data-exec="?/refresh">@(Refresh)</button>
</ui-plugin>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		exports.reload = function() {
			exports.refresh();
		};

		exports.refresh = function() {
			exports.tapi('tasks', function(response) {
				exports.set('items', response);
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

`exports.reload` runs every time the screen opens.

## How does a screen call the server?

With `exports.tapi('endpoint_name', data, callback)`. Add `ERROR` after the name to show an error message to the user by itself:

```js
exports.tapi('tasks_save ERROR', model, function(response) {
	exports.refresh();
});
```

The name is the endpoint of the route: `+tasks_save`.

## What does ? mean in a path?

"This plugin". `?.items` is the data `items` of the plugin, and `?/create` is its function `exports.create`:

```html
<ui-bind path="?.items" config="template"></ui-bind>
<button class="exec" data-exec="?/create">@(Create)</button>
```

## What is CLASS?

A word that is replaced with a class unique to the plugin. Use it in the class of the root and in the selectors of the style, so the CSS of one screen cannot reach another:

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .task { padding: 10px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #E8E8E8; }
</style>

<ui-plugin class="CLASS">
</ui-plugin>
```

## How do I handle the click of a button?

With the class `exec` and `data-exec`. Do not add `onclick` or `addEventListener`:

```html
<button class="exec" data-exec="?/create"><i class="ti ti-plus-circle"></i>@(Create)</button>
<div class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}">{{ m.name }}</div>
```

```js
exports.edit = function(el) {
	var id = ATTRD(el);
};
```

`ATTRD(el)` reads the `data-id` of the element.

## How do I set and read the data of a screen?

`exports.set('items', value)` sets it and the bindings draw it again. `exports.model` is the model of the plugin:

```js
exports.tapi('tasks', function(response) {
	exports.set('items', response);
});
```

## How do I load the jComponent 20 library in a page?

From the CDN, once per document, before the components:

```html
<link href="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<script src="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js"></script>
<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
```

`@{REPO.ui}` is the file of components that `COMPONENTATOR()` made.

## How do I load components?

With `COMPONENTATOR()` in `definitions/init.js`: it downloads the components you name as one file, and the layout loads it with `@{REPO.ui}`.

```js
ON('ready', function() {
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,errorhandler,locale,input,validate,miniform,notify,approve', true);
});
```

List only the components the application uses.

## How do I put a component on a screen?

With `<ui-component>`: its name, the path of its data and its configuration.

```html
<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1;placeholder:@(Relative URL address)">@(URL)</ui-component>
```

## Where do I find a component?

In Componentator, the catalogue of jComponent components: <https://componentator.com>. Look for an existing component before writing a piece of interface by hand. `input` is the one component for every field of a form: its `type` chooses the kind.

## How do I make a form?

A second file, `public/form.html`, with a `miniform`, its inputs, a `validate` that enables the submit button, and a `submit` function:

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;title:@(Redirect);reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1">@(URL)</ui-component>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>
```

## How do I open a form?

The screen loads it with an `importer`, gives it a model and shows it:

```html
<ui-component name="importer" path="common.form" config="if:formredirect;url:/~ID~/form.html"></ui-component>
```

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
```
